stories.Headline: Economists argue AI investment outpaces GDP and may erode demand through falling wage shares
stories.Summary:
Investment in AI-related equipment has grown about 3.5 times since 2021, far faster than GDP, The Hindu reported on November 20, 2026. Indranil Chowdhury and Rohit Azad wrote the piece as the second in a two-part series. They made the global economy their canvas to avoid between-country gain and loss that AI may cause. They asked what may happen to the global pie of output and jobs. They called the piece speculative and presented two opposite cases.

Global demand consists of workers' consumption, capitalists' consumption, investment and government expenditure, because the trade component cancels out. The authors set government intervention outside the "pure" market economy and focused on consumption and investment. They defined the wage share as real wages divided by labour productivity. In their example, output of 100 is split equally, workers consume all their wages and capitalists consume half, giving consumption demand of 75. With AI, the wage share falls to 30%, workers' consumption falls to 30 and capitalists' consumption rises to 35, so demand of 10 disappears.

Rosa Luxemburg, a German Marxist, argued that machines are not an end in themselves. Mikhail Tugan-Baranovsky, a Russian economist, argued that investment can replace lost consumption demand. He went to the extreme to say machines can produce machines which can produce more machines. The authors said the AI case, imagined as machines producing more machines, comes close to what he had in mind. Luxemburg said unsold goods pile in warehouses, machines lie idle and investment contracts.

The authors listed counter-tendencies: productivity may rise in AI sectors while demand grows in low-productivity sectors, wages may rise in proportion, or investment demand may replace lost consumption demand. They said the bulk of AI investment would show up under computers and peripherals. In their index starting at 100 in 2021, nominal GDP rose 1.5 times while AI investment rose 3.5 times in less than two years. AI in the chart is expenditures on "Computers and peripheral equipment", and 2026 Q3 is BEA's advance estimate.

The authors said they had not touched the ecological crisis AI may lead to in electricity generation and water usage. They said the global North may push the crisis to the South by setting up data centres there. They said some countries may gain at the expense of others. They said the slowdown can be arrested through aggressive government expenditure, such as universal basic income or military spending, particularly in the global North. They said the whole AI phenomenon may be a stock market bubble like the dotcom or subprime bubble.

The authors said heavy investments were made expecting higher AI profits and financed in the US primarily through debt. They said debt will pile up the further off the profit-making phase is. They said if profits do not match expectations, debts will not be honoured and a domino effect may follow, much like the subprime crisis. They said rising interest rates, in an effort to target inflation induced by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, may raise debt burdens further. They cited Hyman Minsky's Ponzi finance and the collapse of Lehman Brothers, which triggered the 2008 global financial crisis.

stories.Headline: Dutch regulator warns consumers not to buy AI camera glasses after tests find dangerous errors
stories.Summary:
The Dutch Data Protection Authority officially warned consumers on Thursday, 19 November 2026, not to buy AI camera glasses after examining six types of camera glasses available in the Netherlands. The watchdog found that the glasses, which have a microphone that lets users ask questions to an AI chatbot, pose major privacy risks and can be actively dangerous because the responses are often incorrect. In one test the AP simulated an emergency in which someone was being resuscitated and asked the glasses for help, and the glasses said they had called the emergency number 112 and that an ambulance was on its way. That was an AI hallucination, because the glasses had made no such call. In other tests the glasses gave dating advice to an adult interested in a child, made errors when interpreting medication leaflets, and wrongly read the safety warning on toys.

The warning requires consumers to think carefully before buying these devices, and the AP recommended banning the glasses in sensitive locations like hospitals and sports clubs, where many organizations have already implemented such a ban. The AP had previously warned owners of AI camera glasses that secretly recording people is a crime. Monique Verdier, the AP vice-chair, said glasses that record you without your knowledge are concerning enough, but glasses that also provide incorrect advice when someone's life is at stake go a step too far. She said that while AI offers many opportunities, we must be able to trust the technology, and in the case of the camera glasses examined, such trust is currently not justified.

Civil rights organization Bits of Freedom called the new AP warning too little, too late. Evelyn Austin, the executive director of Bits of Freedom, told ANP that it is a bit like the Dutch Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority advising people not to eat a dangerous product rather than simply removing the contaminated food from the shelves. She said it is completely backwards, that the AP has one clear mandate to protect citizens by enforcing privacy laws, and that the authority is failing to do so. She said these peeping glasses should be pulled from the market.

stories.Headline: Blacklisted Chinese universities buy restricted Nvidia AI chips through obscure suppliers
stories.Summary:
At least six blacklisted Chinese universities bought restricted Nvidia AI chips through obscure suppliers, according to a CNN analysis released on July 19. Two universities closely affiliated with the Chinese military acquired high performance chips in just the past few months. These institutions used little known Chinese companies rather than Nvidia or large distributors to obtain the hardware. The analysis examined approximately 300 procurement notices from Chinese universities collected in a commercial database. Most of these notices involved purchases of restricted chips including the A100, A800, H100, H200, and H800.

The Harbin Institute of Technology bought one A100 chip for about 7,000 dollars in September. Northwestern Polytechnical University purchased four H200 chips for 240,000 dollars over two occasions in September and October. Beihang University, blacklisted since 2001, bought A100 and A800 chips about ten times from 2022 to 2024. Since last December, the United States allowed H200 sales on a case by case basis with a 25 percent tariff. The Commerce Department approved over 800,000 chips for Chinese firms by May 11, including 150,000 for Tencent.

Gregory Allen of Decision Tree Research said these universities are closely connected to the Chinese military and invest in military AI. Mao Ning from the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs said China opposes the United States for overstretching national security concepts. Kate Koren of CSIS noted that some chips might have come from inventory stockpiled before 2022 controls. She stated that smuggling is difficult to detect because it involves shell companies, document forgery, and multiple countries. Koren admitted that some chips will slip through even if the United States does its best.

The purchases affect the United States government, which requires suppliers to verify end users to prevent chips flowing into China. Lawmakers revealed the Commerce Department approved chips for Alibaba, which has ties to a military linked laboratory. Other approved sales included 43,000 chips for Baidu and 4,000 for the carmaker BYD. Nvidia applied in April to sell 40,000 H200 chips to New Century Lettall Data Service, tied to Megaspeed. This company is linked to Alice Huang, an executive identified by United States intelligence as a Chinese asset.

The A100 chip remains banned, but it was widely sold in China before the 2022 export controls. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned last week after his relationship with Alice Huang was revealed. The Donald Trump administration introduced new regulations this week to block bypass routes using overseas data centers. Chinese companies previously leased semiconductors from data centers in Malaysia, Indonesia, and Thailand to avoid these restrictions. The Bureau of Industry and Security has launched an official investigation into Moonshot AI's access routes.

Moonshot AI canceled a 150 million dollar contract with an Indonesian provider to secure Blackwell Ultra B300 semiconductors. New rules require data centers providing resources above a certain level to Chinese customers to get permission within 90 days. Sidley Austin says this threshold corresponds to about 300 advanced AI semiconductors, while contracts often involve thousands. Bernstein reports that the cost of training AI models for Chinese companies is highly likely to rise. It remains open whether the chips listed in the procurement notices were actually delivered to the universities.

stories.Headline: Trump trades Nvidia shares heavily before Jensen Huang resigns amid spy scandal
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump traded Nvidia shares heavily before a scandal involving former CEO Jensen Huang broke in November 2026. Trump bought and sold these stocks repeatedly to seek trading gains until weeks before the affair scandal erupted. The former chief executive stepped down on November 12 after admitting to an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang. Alice Huang has been alleged to be a Chinese spy, which created a crisis for the chipmaker. This sequence of events led to significant scrutiny regarding the timing of the president's financial activities.

In August, Trump bought as much as 1.6 million dollars of stock and sold 1 million dollars of shares. During September, he bought up to 265,000 dollars and sold 15,000 dollars of Nvidia stock, according to ethics filings. By the end of August, his holdings were worth between 13 million and 62 million dollars in Washington. This was a sharp increase from the end of 2024, when holdings were between 615,000 and 1.3 million dollars. On January 6, Trump bought as much as 1 million dollars of shares before signing an executive order.

White House spokesman Davis Ingle stated that third-party financial institutions independently manage the president's portfolio and track the Schwab 1000. He added that neither Trump nor any family member has the authority to direct or influence these investments. Regarding Alice Huang, Trump said she may not be a spy and claimed national security was never in danger. He asserted that the country is stronger now than ever before while defending the former executive's private life. The administration dismissed all conflict-of-interest concerns surrounding the purchases and sales of the semiconductor company's shares.

Senate Democratic floor leader Chuck Schumer said the president should protect the United States rather than China or his friends. He criticized Trump for defending Jensen Huang instead of safeguarding national security and called for a full congressional investigation. Chinese AI companies are affected, as Z.AI tumbled over 10 percent and MiniMax hit record lows in Hong Kong. Hardware suppliers Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink Technology slumped, while the Hang Seng Tech Index dropped 3 percent on Friday. Investors fear the US will reduce sourcing from Chinese suppliers and tighten restrictions on advanced chip access.

Trump previously announced on Truth Social last December that he would permit sales of H200 AI chips to China. He signed a related executive order on January 14, following his million dollar stock purchase in early January. Trump and Huang had appeared together at the White House on April 30, 2025, to discuss US investment. They also stood together on October 8 at the U.S. Institute of Peace for the National Medal of Science. These interactions established a close relationship that has drawn persistent scrutiny over potential conflicts of interest.

The US House Speaker Mike Johnson noted a growing consensus in Congress to limit chip exports to China. The presidents of the US and China are due to meet next week in Shenzhen at the APEC summit. Some analysts expect tighter export controls by the end of this year to limit Chinese access to compute. Jensen Huang is reportedly exploring a return to Nvidia amid a campaign of support from the Silicon Valley community. The articles leave open whether Congress will successfully investigate the administration's failure to counter foreign espionage targeting technology.

stories.Headline: Meta rethinks its 2030 net-zero deadline as 2025 emissions rise 45%
stories.Summary:
Meta Platforms posted its 2026 Sustainability Report on Thursday, November 19, 2026, and said it is rethinking the 2030 deadline for its net-zero goal. The report said Meta's 2025 net emissions rose to 11.8 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent, up 45% from 2024. Meta's stock closed Friday, November 20, at $560.84, down 5.93%, during a broad tech selloff. Shares fell 11.6% over the past week, then traded at $569.32 after hours. Meta set the goal in 2020: net zero across its whole value chain, plus water positive, by 2030.

Meta says it matched 100% of its electricity with clean and renewable energy for the sixth straight year. Direct Scope 1 emissions were just 33,555 tons, and market-based Scope 2 purchased power was 10,861 tons. Scope 3 amounted to 11,858,913 tons, about 99% of the total. Capital goods such as servers, chips, networking gear, steel and concrete made up 73%, and clean power contracts do little to reduce them. By the article's calculation, electricity use rose 34.9% to 24,849,122 megawatt-hours, and data centers used 24,523,035 of that.

Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability, wrote in the report's opening letter that Meta is "re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones." They said AI demand grew faster than almost anyone projected, and clean energy fell behind because of years-long grid interconnection waiting lines, slow permitting, and lagging transmission. Meta says its long-term dreams are unchanged, but it gave no date for a revised plan. Mark Zuckerberg spoke on the October 21, 2026 earnings call and said Muse is "very compute-intensive to run" and that "we have not launched it globally yet." Third-quarter capex was $34.906 billion, up 85.38%, and free cash flow was -$2.120 billion.

Alphabet, Google's parent company, faces the same pressure, having pledged in 2020 to run on carbon-free energy by 2030. Google stopped saying carbon-neutral operations by 2024 and has acknowledged that its emissions are still rising. By the article's math, 2025 Scope 3 was about 2.05 times the 5,772,583-ton 2021 baseline Meta aims not to exceed by end-2031. Reaching it would require cleaner suppliers or slower building. The climate reset adds some image and regulatory exposure, and the bigger question for the stock is whether the expansion pays off.

Meta still guides 2026 capex to $135 billion to $145 billion. Third-quarter revenue rose 26.07%, and the stock trades at a P/E of 21, which the article calls reasonable for that growth. For comparison, Alphabet already shows AI spending turning into sales, as Google Cloud revenue rose 103%. The interconnection waiting lines and permitting delays that slowed clean energy also limit how fast new data centers can come online. The article says the core business is paying for the expansion so far.

The test for this view is Meta's fourth-quarter call, where it will give 2027 capex guidance. If capex rises again while fourth-quarter revenue comes in below the $73 billion low end of guidance, the case for the expansion weakens. The articles leave open what a revised net-zero plan would contain, since Meta gave no date for one. They also leave open whether cleaner suppliers or slower building could bring Scope 3 back to the 2021 baseline by end-2031. stories.Headline: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 per share ahead of Nasdaq debut
stories.Summary:
Anthropic announced on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, that it will sell stock at $83 per share, and the company behind the Claude chatbot is expected to go public on Thursday. The San Francisco-based firm will trade under the ticker symbol “ANT,” and the price is above a previously expected range of $70 to $78. The IPO will raise $81 billion with a valuation of about $1.5 trillion, a level well above $1 trillion. Anthropic earned $16.3 billion in revenue over the first six months of this year, growing nearly 14-fold from the same period a year earlier, according to a government filing. Still, the company reported a net loss of $80.7 billion over the first six months of this year, indicating the scale of its spending over that period.

The IPO pulls in fresh funds for the San Francisco-based firm, which aims to compete in a potentially lucrative but cost-intensive section of the AI industry centered on advanced models and the tools they empower. The Nasdaq issued a rule change in May permitting “fast entry” to the Nasdaq-100 for some major IPOs, and over the ensuing weeks some other top exchanges also tweaked their rules, though their eligibility requirements vary. Anthropic will all but certainly become a part of people’s 401(k) accounts soon, because those accounts often hold index funds pegged to major indexes like the Nasdaq. Until recently, newly listed companies were barred from major indexes until after an extended waiting period. A financial filing last month presents AI as “one of the most consequential technologies in human history,” saying that if managed well it could rapidly accelerate scientific innovation, greatly increase economic growth rates, bring cures for major diseases within reach, and solve problems that have resisted generations of human effort.

In the same document, Anthropic warned of the possibility its AI models could pose a “catastrophic or existential risk to humanity,” and it added that investing in the company’s stock “involves a high degree of risk.” Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse made the point directly that money left crypto to buy Anthropic IPO shares, which had nothing to do with Ripple. VanEck’s Matthew Sigel described it as a capital vacuum draining every coin at once. The XRP price trades near $0.95 on November 21, after touching $0.89 on November 15, its lowest level since November 2024, and the cause is outside the token itself. Spot XRP ETFs lost $19.13 million in the week to November 13, the largest weekly outflow since March.

Traders keep naming $1 as roughly this cycle’s floor, and most of them hold $10 as the long-run XRP price prediction, which from $0.95 is about 950% upside. The math is simple: $10 on 63.5 billion tokens gives a market cap near $635 billion, a level the largest crypto assets have already reached. XRP fell from $3.84 in 2018 to $0.11 by 2020, then climbed back to $3.84 in 2025, and the weekly RSI divergence forming now is the first chart sign that selling pressure is easing. Taking XRP from a $60.6 billion valuation to $10 needs about $575 billion of new money, and a move like that takes years. Pepeto released a security upgrade for its exchange this week, and within days the presale passed $11.29 million in the same month XRP had its worst run in two years.

Pepeto is a meme coin on Ethereum, built by an original Pepe cofounder, and the difference is simple: Pepe came with a joke, while Pepeto comes with trading tools. This upgrade protects the AI risk scorer, which deals with a problem most traders still have, because they buy without checking the contract and some tokens let a buyer in but never let them sell. The scanner checks a coin before your money moves and blocks a trap token before it leaves your wallet, so the money that would have been lost stays with you. Pepeto at the presale price is valued near $80 million, so a small part of that money moves it much further. If it reached just half of Pepe’s $11.4 billion record, that would be about 71 times today’s price, and a $1,000 entry would turn into roughly $71,300.

That same $1,000 buys you about 5.27 billion PEPETO today, and staking starts the moment you buy and pays around $1,600 a year at today’s rate while you wait for the listing. The catalyst for that move is the approaching Binance listing, and stages are closing faster every week, with the entry price climbing each time one fills. Addresses tied to large XRP holdings have taken positions far too big to be test buys, and investors with that kind of history do not commit at that size unless they expect a return. The XRP price, and the money leaving crypto for the Anthropic IPO, explain what the wider market is doing this week, and they also explain why the addresses with the longest track record chose to enter now instead of waiting. The articles leave open the exact date of the Binance listing and the final valuation Anthropic will reach when it begins trading on Thursday.

stories.Headline: Suregiant Technology expands capacity to target AI advanced packaging market
stories.Summary:
Suregiant Technology held a pre-OTC-listing earnings presentation on November 18, 2026, to discuss its growth. The company targets high-double-digit growth as its release film enters the advanced packaging market. This material is now used in mass production for the world's top five semiconductor manufacturers. The company is expanding its capacity to meet the rising demand for AI chip packaging. These developments aim to drive revenue and profit to new highs for the firm.

Taoyuan Plant 2 will start official mass production in December, with a scale 2.5 to 3 times Plant 1. The company expects a full-year capacity contribution in 2027 and an OTC listing in mid-December. The tentative public offering price is NT$438 per share for the upcoming listing on the market. Release film entered 2.5D packaging in 2024, FOPLP processes in 2025, and 3D advanced packaging in 2026. The company's first three quarters of 2026 saw earnings per share reach NT$6.35 for investors.

Chairman Yang Yun-pin stated that order visibility extends 2 to 3 years for the company. He noted that customer forecast orders have reached 5 to 6 years for their products. Yang explained that their precision coating experience allows them to provide customized samples to major manufacturers. He said the company does not rely on one customer because end customers are highly diversified. Yang believes long-term demand remains solid as the overall AI and high-end packaging megatrend continues.

Institutional investors noted that AI and high-performance computing demand is expanding the advanced packaging market. Yole Group estimates this market will grow from $46.1 billion in 2024 to $79.4 billion by 2030. First-tier manufacturers are affected as they expand capacity for molding and wafer grinding using these materials. Japanese manufacturers previously dominated this segment, but Suregiant is now capturing share through localized service capabilities. The company's products are already supplied for mass production use in first-tier advanced packaging plants.

Suregiant started in the optoelectronics industry and entered the semiconductor field in 2014 to build material expertise. The company currently focuses on two major product lines, which are release film and grinding tape. Grinding tape has been supplied to the world's top ten packaging plants for more than 12 years. Third-quarter revenue was NT$159 million, which represents an 80.76 percent increase over the previous quarter. After-tax net profit for the third quarter was NT$66.51 million, up 92.72 percent quarter-on-quarter.

A new-generation thick grinding tape is expected to begin contributing to company revenue in 2027. Official samples for a new hydrolyzable tape are expected to be sent to customers in mid-2027. This new tape may begin a gradual ramp-up in 2028 as the company's third growth leg. The articles leave open whether Taiwanese firms can continue capturing market share from Japanese material suppliers. Future performance depends on the ramp-up speed of Plant 2 and the verification of new products.

stories.Headline: AI chip developers shift HBM production to a shared design and manufacturing model
stories.Summary:
NVIDIA unveiled its Custom HBM platform called NVHBM in August 2026 to integrate into the NVLink Fusion lineup for AI accelerators. This new platform will be deployed in NVIDIA's own Feynman GPU and also within AWS's Trainium 4 AI hardware. In October, Marvell presented a system for custom HBM at the OCP Global Summit to discuss new design tradeoffs. This shift moves the industry from a memory maker led model toward a three way division of labor for production. Memory makers like Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron previously controlled both the design and manufacturing of the entire HBM stack.

The new layout moves the memory controller into a custom base die beneath each DRAM stack instead of on the XPU. A narrower die to die physical interface replaces the wide HBM interface at the XPU edge to connect the components. Marvell estimates this change provides up to 25 percent more compute area and room for 33 percent more HBM stacks. Memory interface power could be 70 percent lower, while adaptive power management reduces interface power by 75 percent under normal workloads. These changes shift base die production to advanced logic processes, which increases the importance of TSMC in the supply chain.

Marvell stated that no single company can build custom HBM alone because it requires a coordinated effort from several partners. They argued that the base die, die to die interface, and package thermals must be co designed as one system. Marvell noted that the die to die PHY is a heat hotspot, making package cooling a central design constraint. They suggested using silicon heat paths, copper to copper hybrid bonding, or coolant channels etched into silicon to manage heat. Marvell also mentioned that adaptive power management can reduce interface power by 42 percent during periods of peak traffic.

AI chip developers are evaluating custom HBM because standard HBM must prioritize compatibility, which leaves limited room for individual accelerator optimization. GPU and ASIC designers are now helping define the foundation of HBM, which affects how these critical AI components function. IBM Technology's Kaoutar El Maghraoui explained that some workloads are limited by memory bandwidth rather than by the available computing capacity. This means adding more compute area may not speed up tasks if data movement remains the primary bottleneck for workloads. Marvell cited a Samsung study showing internal thermal resistance accounts for 57 percent of the HBM stack's total resistance.

HBM has traditionally been the home turf for memory makers who controlled everything from DRAM dies to the bottom base die. Marvell estimates HBM now takes up roughly 30 percent of a typical AI accelerator die area in the current market. At 2026 memory prices, HBM accounts for more than half of the total cost of a typical XPU AI accelerator. The roofline model and arithmetic intensity are used to distinguish whether a workload is constrained by compute or memory bandwidth. Samsung's thermal study also found that internal thermal resistance accounts for 13 percent of the total for an adjacent ASIC.

Custom HBM appears to be on the final stretch toward mass production as developers continue to evaluate these new design options. For next generation HBM running above 28 Gbps, Marvell expects the heat flux to exceed 2.0 watts per square millimeter. Marvell relays a projection that internal temperatures in 16 high HBM stacks will exceed the thermal budget by the year 2028. TrendForce will provide more insights on HBM and custom ASICs at the Roadshow Japan 2026 event in Tokyo on December 8. The articles leave open how fast CPO will scale and how a split US China market will reshape 2027 servers.

stories.Headline: Viz.ai and rural health group run AI education events for hospitals
stories.Summary:
Viz.ai and the National Rural Health Association held three educational events for rural health systems since their partnership began in April, according to Viz.ai Chief Clinical Officer Andrew Ibrahim, M.D., who spoke with Fierce Healthcare at HLTH. The partnership, almost seven months old as of the Nov. 18, 2026 article, aims to help rural healthcare leaders better understand and implement AI tools across systems. Ibrahim discussed the collaboration at HLTH 2026, the conference held over four days in Las Vegas, where executives walked in on Nov. 16, 2026. The HLTH 2026 takeaways article, published Nov. 20, 2026 by Rebecca Pifer Parduhn and Jill Hughes, reported that AI and affordability dominated the conference. Healthcare is AI's largest vertical market, with spending hitting $3.7 billion this year, according to Menlo Ventures.

The educational series aims to show rural health administrators the specifics of AI and whether they should adopt it, Ibrahim said. He noted there is sometimes a very big mismatch when smaller rural health systems onboard multiple vendors. Ibrahim said many rural hospitals lack the IT expertise and infrastructure to adopt some of these tools, making the effort a force function to strengthen their hub-and-spoke relationships. Strengthening these relationships has been key, and Ibrahim said it has been beautiful to see. The partnership is approaching its one-year mark.

Ibrahim said the collaboration has been a personal and professional passion of his. He described the mismatch smaller rural systems face when onboarding multiple vendors. He said the events aim to show administrators the specifics of AI and whether to adopt it. He said many rural hospitals lack the IT expertise and infrastructure for some tools. He said strengthening hub-and-spoke relationships has been key.

At HLTH, Google Cloud global healthcare director Aashima Gupta described an industry paradox, saying that while the raw token price is declining, token consumption is exploding and on the rise. Elevance chief digital information officer Ratnakar Lavu said every market will see costs increasing in the short term as many things are built. Dr. Brian Anderson, CEO of the Coalition for Health AI, said every digital health invention has increased the digital divide and increased cost. OpenAI announced partnerships aimed at accelerating computer-use agents, a subset of agentic AI that see a screen, simulate mouse clicks and traverse tasks using visual cues, with plans to apply agentic workflows to insurance preapprovals and discharge planning. Suki launched an agentic operating system aimed at reducing complexity across administrative workflows, and Amazon Web Services announced new agentic capabilities in Amazon Health Connect enabling patients to book appointments, verify identities and manage prescriptions.

AWS general manager and director of healthcare AI Naji Shafi said the University of California San Diego reportedly cut down 630 hours of staff phone time weekly after implementing AWS' identification verification capability, and the number of calls abandoned dropped about 30%. Dan Mendelson, CEO of Morgan Health, said employers would love to cover GLP-1s but find them unbearably expensive, and employers wake up one morning and it is 5% of their total medical expense. Dr. Lisa Shah, chief medical officer at Twin Health, said two-thirds of people on GLP-1s stop taking them within a year due to side effects. Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., said during a Sunday session that we have got to stop the bleeding, after Democrats took the House and Senate in the midterm elections earlier this month. Amy Perry, CEO of Phoenix-based nonprofit system Banner Health, said Arizonans losing health insurance has been Banner's biggest headwind over the last year.

Blue Shield of California CEO Mike Stuart said success to him looks like more people have coverage in 2028 than they did in 2027. Dr. Ezekiel Emanuel, a former healthcare advisor to the Obama administration, and Brian Blase, president of the conservative Paragon Health Institute, agreed during a Tuesday main stage session that reforming the No Surprises Act and enacting site-neutral hospital payments are good ideas for improving affordability. Blase said Congress is subject to lobbying and there is no stronger lobby than the healthcare industry. Sesame co-founder Dr. Michael Botta said GLP-1s may feel unique for now but this is the start of it, not the end. AARP CEO Dr. Myechia Minter-Jordan said during a Monday panel that fifty for many of us is just halfway there and aging is everybody's business.

Thom Bales, health services sector lead at PwC, said health plans are taking a hard look at medical necessity and pulling back, driving renewed interest in value-based care, targeting benefits to specific populations and alternative arrangements like ICHRAs. Mendelson said he firmly believes insurance will still be around in 10 years but it will look really different, and asked whether large insurance companies will still be around or face a Kodak moment. Botta said ultimately he thinks that is where we are headed, with people paying some type of membership or subscription fee to their doctor and using insurance for the big stuff like a hospitalization, a surgery, an accident or a chronic disease diagnosis. Roughly 150 million Americans are over the age of 50 and generate $12.5 trillion for the U.S. economy each year, according to AARP. There is a gap of about 12.5 years between how long Americans live and how many of those years are actually healthy.

stories.Headline: Investors buy Anthropic IPO as tech stocks and chipmakers face a broad sell-off
stories.Summary:
Investors piled into the initial public offering of Anthropic on Thursday, which saw the company storm onto the public markets. This event occurred while tech stocks and chipmakers faced a broad sell-off, creating a disconnect for those investing in AI. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2 percent, and the S&P 500 logged another ugly day during this period. Chip stocks were bleeding, and companies like Nvidia and AMD were getting crushed as the market faced a perfect storm. Selling pressure extended into Friday, November 20, 2026, as investors began repricing the AI trade in real time.

The Nasdaq Composite closed at 23,020.97, while the S&P 500 fell to 7,021.68 and the Dow 30 dropped to 48,769.04. Anthropic, PBC shares were at 84.70, and Nvidia Corporation fell to 135.32, while Intel Corporation dropped to 52.59 on Friday. CoreWeave reported nearly 90 billion dollars in debt and liabilities, alongside a net loss of 709 million dollars in the third quarter. Nvidia reported 116 billion dollars in third-quarter revenue, 65 billion dollars in net income, 32 billion dollars in debt, and 118 billion liabilities. The Russell 2000 fell to 2,608.41, and the VIX rose to 32.10, while Bitcoin USD dropped to 58,906.46.

Executive Editor Brian Sozzi said the market is facing a perfect storm where investors are less willing to pay any price. He noted that the Democratic Blue Wave has Wall Street questioning if Washington will put brakes on AI and data center construction. Sozzi stated that the leadership fallout at Nvidia is shaking confidence, as the market does not like interim CEO Collect Crest. He mentioned that technical selling and market clearing events are forcing investors to raise cash during this period of volatility. Sozzi also cited sticky inflation, hawkish Fed rhetoric, and the prospect of tighter financial conditions as drivers of the current weakness.

Hyperscalers including Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle are no longer cash-flow positive despite the billions they reap in quarterly revenue. Neoclouds, which rent compute to hyperscalers, are tens of billions in debt, with CoreWeave seeing its stock price drop over 50 percent. Short seller reports targeting AMD and fresh regulatory fears regarding China have further damaged the semiconductor trade and affected these specific chipmakers. Bethany McLean questioned if the hundreds of billions spent on AI infrastructure and data centers can be repaid when it is due. Investors who want the AI future are now facing a reality where the broader AI trade is being blown to pieces.

Nvidia previously operated under an open checkbook policy led by founder Jensen Huang, who was the face of the AI revolution. The company loaned money to neoclouds to buy Nvidia chips, a tactic that critics have described as circular financing. Nvidia essentially guaranteed it would cover the debt of neoclouds if they could not pay, making Nvidia the guarantor of last resort. Much of this debt was resold to Wall Street and held by insurance companies, creating a complex web of financial liabilities. The industry has seen aggressive financial practices and rapid data center construction that may now be reined in by new leadership.

The market is waiting for Nvidia to announce a permanent CEO, as there is currently no timeline for this specific leadership decision. Investors are watching to see if the Democratic wave will burst the AI bubble and who will be left holding debt. It remains open whether the AI dream can survive the current repricing and the potential for tighter financial conditions from the Fed. The situation leaves it unclear if Anthropic can maintain its status as a 2 trillion dollar sensation amid the broader sell-off. Future market movements depend on regulatory fears in China and the ability of neoclouds to manage their massive debt loads.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh has made understanding artificial intelligence’s effects on the economy a priority, creating a task force to examine the issue as he tries to reshape how the central bank sets monetary policy. The minutes from the Federal Reserve’s October board meeting showed that nearly all officials raised concerns about negative consequences to the financial system if AI yields disappointing results. Policymakers and Wall Street are also becoming increasingly concerned about what could happen if the AI boom fails to deliver on its promises. The October meeting minutes record that nearly all officials flagged the risk that disappointing AI results could harm the financial system, a concern shared by policymakers and Wall Street.

Warsh has created a task force to examine AI’s economic effects and has said the Fed is modeling various scenarios on what the impact might be. stories.Headline: Legora adds Teams legal intake and Microsoft 365 AI search
stories.Summary:
Legora added legal request intake in Microsoft Teams and AI search across Outlook and Calendar to its Microsoft 365 offering, and the features are now generally available, IT Brief Australia reported on 20 November 2026. Staff can submit legal requests by tagging @Legora in Teams, while lawyers can search relevant email and meeting context from Microsoft 365 as they prepare responses and next steps. Existing user permissions remain in place when lawyers use the tools. The update expands Legora's existing Microsoft integrations, which include SharePoint, OneDrive and a plug-in for Copilot for Legal. It is intended to reduce the time legal teams spend gathering background material from chats, inboxes, calendars and documents before they can begin substantive work.

Legora's Teams intake tool allows a request to begin in the collaboration platform and flow into its legal workflow, and lawyers can then use the Microsoft 365 search function within Legora to identify relevant emails and calendar information linked to the matter. Lawyers can use that context to help draft a response and prepare follow-up actions, and check source material as needed. Legora's SharePoint integration remains in beta and allows the system to use stored documents to support agreement review and save edits back to SharePoint as a new version. Its plug-in for Copilot for Legal is generally available and allows users to begin legal work from Microsoft 365 Copilot. Legora said its products are used by more than 140,000 legal professionals at more than 2,500 law firms and in-house legal teams across more than 80 markets.

Max Junestrand, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of Legora, said legal work is shifting from executing tasks to directing them and standing behind the results. He said that only holds up if requests arrive with context and stay inside the controls legal teams already trust. He said that with Microsoft, Legora is making that possible, so legal professionals can spend more of their time on the judgment their stakeholders depend on them for. Tom Quoroll, Partner at Linklaters, said ensuring that its use of AI enhances the quality that Linklaters' clients expect is central to its strategy. Quoroll said Legora's integration with the wealth of Microsoft 365 context transforms its lawyers' ability to leverage that data, and that Linklaters is excited to connect two of the most powerful tools in its technology stack.

Samer Abu-Ltaif, President, Microsoft EMEA, said Legora is a great example of the bold AI innovation changing how legal work gets done, and that Microsoft is proud to help bring its solutions to lawyers around the world. He said Microsoft's customers want AI that works where they already work, and that Legora helps legal teams move from intake to finished work with relevant organizational context, ensuring enterprise security and governance. He said it is a clear example of how Microsoft's partner ecosystem turns AI into real impact. Linklaters, which uses the software, said the integration could help its lawyers make more direct use of information held within Microsoft 365. In practice, legal requests often reach in-house teams and law firms through several channels at once, including chat messages, emails and meetings, and supporting material may then sit across Outlook inboxes, calendar entries and document libraries, requiring lawyers to re-enter requests, forward files or create copies in separate systems.

Profound announced Profound for Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365, together with new integrations that connect Your AI Marketer in Profound to SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook and Microsoft Work IQ, GlobeNewswire reported from New York on 19 November 2026. By mentioning @Profound in a channel or messaging it directly, teams can ask what changed in their AI Search visibility, accuracy and citation share, why it changed, and what to do about it. From the same Teams message, they can create and run agents or start a new Profound Project, then use the Open project button to jump directly to the work, and they can also open direct-message conversations in Profound to continue working there. Your AI Marketer in Profound can find and read files in SharePoint and OneDrive, create and edit Word and Excel documents, bring selected SharePoint content into a Profound Knowledge Base and Context Manager, read email and write drafts in the connected user's Outlook mailbox, send completed reports from Outlook, and draw on a user's Microsoft 365 work context through Microsoft Work IQ. Everything Profound produces is reviewed and approved by the team before it goes live.

James Cadwallader, CEO and Co-founder of Profound, said marketing teams should not have to leave the conversation to get an answer or get work moving. He said Microsoft 365 is where much of that work already happens, so building on it was the natural choice, and that Your AI Marketer in Profound sits alongside the team, works from the content they already have and hands back results where they will be used. Sujeet Meha, VP of Teams Engineering, Microsoft, said AI is most useful when people can put it to work in the tools they already rely on. He said Profound's integration with Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365 gives marketing teams a way to connect their AI marketing workflows with the conversations, documents and information they use every day, and that it is a practical example of how companies can extend Microsoft 365 to help people get more done. Profound for Microsoft Teams is available now to customers with an active Profound subscription and can be installed directly from the Microsoft Marketplace.

stories.Headline: The Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation pledges 350 million dollars in computing spending to CoreWeave
stories.Summary:
The Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation will provide 350 million dollars in computing spending to the company known as CoreWeave. This financial commitment was revealed in recent tax disclosures from the charitable organization established by the former Nvidia chief executive officer. A filing from Nvidia in June identified CoreWeave as the receiver and noted that 108.3 million dollars were already spent. The funding supports the Computing Initiative for Open Science to give researchers access to large scale GPU computing resources. This specific pledge represents the largest donation made by the Huang Foundation during the 2025 calendar year.

The foundation gave 19 million dollars to the California College of the Arts and 1.2 million dollars to the Hong Kong University. Core Scientific is building a 100 megawatt data center at Port Muskogee, Oklahoma, under a broader 500 megawatt hosting agreement. This wider arrangement with CoreWeave has a potential value of 8.7 billion dollars over twelve years with two five year extensions. The Muskogee site uses 70 megawatts for critical IT capacity and 30 megawatts for cooling and electrical systems. Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company serves as the electricity provider for this facility which began construction in early 2025.

CoreWeave stated that the charitable foundation does not directly use the computing power provided through these specific financial grants. The foundation is responsible for awarding resources to scientific research grant awardees who then utilize the large scale GPU computing. Core Scientific manages the Muskogee project with Evans General Contractors serving as the construction manager under a cost plus fee contract. The project design includes two compute data halls and one separate network data hall to accommodate high density GPU equipment. These facilities will support high performance computing workloads for CoreWeave and one end customer who remains undisclosed to the public.

Investors are scrutinizing the financial interactions between AI infrastructure firms and consumers because the sector is now heavily financially intertwined. CoreWeave investors view the foundation pledge as a sign of more demand for computing services and the necessary GPU hardware. Port Muskogee estimates the data center will generate 4 billion dollars in capital investment and 182 million dollars in benefits. Local entities including Muskogee County, the City of Muskogee, and Hilldale School District may receive 12 million dollars in tax revenue. The project is expected to support 150 jobs with average salaries that exceed 65,000 dollars for the local workforce.

The foundation assets were 12.7 billion dollars at December 31, 2025, which is an increase from the previous 9.2 billion dollars. About 90 percent of these assets consist of Nvidia shares, and the organization gave 373 million dollars in 2024. CoreWeave relies on powerful GPUs for its cloud computing company, and Nvidia is a key stakeholder in the business. This expansion is part of a wider US buildout, including Oracle's 165 billion dollar Project Jupiter planned for New Mexico. Core Scientific is converting and developing infrastructure to serve the growing demand for AI and cloud computing across the country.

The Muskogee facility was initially anticipated to reach substantial completion during the first half of the 2026 calendar year. Investors will continue to scrutinize future disclosures regarding the remaining computing obligations and the revenue contributions for the firm CoreWeave. stories.Headline: Google gives IIT Kharagpur $5 million to fund AI research and education
stories.Summary:
Google announced on November 21, 2026, that it would give IIT Kharagpur $5 million, or Rs 46 crore, for advanced AI research, education and technology development. Google made the announcement through its official blog. Google CEO Sundar Pichai, an IIT Kharagpur alumnus, announced the initiative as part of the company's efforts to support AI research and develop scientific and technical talent in India. The funding will help the institute's researchers and students work on AI-based solutions. The grant covers AI applications in Indian languages, agriculture, materials science and educational technology, and AI training for students, faculty members and teachers.

The funding focuses on three main areas: advanced AI research, educational opportunities and AI capacity building across the institute. Under the research component, projects will use AI to address real-world challenges in Indic languages, materials science, agriculture and educational technology. The focus on Indic languages aims to support AI solutions that work across India's diverse language landscape. The second part will expand AI learning through training programmes and curriculum for students, faculty members and teachers. The third area will strengthen IIT Kharagpur's AI capabilities through AI frameworks and tools for its technological ecosystem and campus research.

Pichai said IIT Kharagpur is doing important work in areas such as Indic languages, agriculture and education. He said the collaboration would help accelerate this work and create opportunities for the next generation of students. Pichai also said India is increasingly at the forefront of innovation. He said initiatives like this can help make the benefits of AI accessible to people across the country. The aim is to help more people gain AI knowledge and skills and prepare the next generation of scientific and technical talent.

A meta-analysis involving 14,321 participants found positive learning outcomes for intelligent tutoring systems compared with conventional large-group instruction (Ma et al., 2014). A randomized study of 194 university physics students found a carefully designed AI tutor produced greater short-term learning gains in less time than comparison classroom-based active-learning instruction (Kestin et al., 2025). In a randomized experiment with nearly 1,000 high school mathematics students, those using unrestricted GPT-4 performed 48 percent better during practice but scored 17 percent lower on later independent examinations without AI than the control group (Bastani et al., 2025). Stanford University's November 2026 SCALE review synthesized 52 causal studies and found promising outcomes from interactive tutoring, adaptive instruction, sequenced practice and feedback, while warning that using AI to complete academic work can undermine independent performance (Walker et al., 2026). In Stanford's Tutor CoPilot experiment, more than 700 tutors and over 1,000 students took part, and students whose tutors received AI assistance were 4 percentage points more likely to master mathematics topics, with gains of 9 percentage points among students working with lower-rated tutors (Wang et al., 2025).

The articles say education is not measured by how quickly learners finish assignments but by how deeply they understand and independently apply knowledge. They say AI's educational value depends less on technological sophistication than on how teachers and students use it. They say apparent academic improvement may sometimes reflect dependence rather than competence. They say favorable student attitudes toward AI did not consistently translate into measurable learning gains. They say teachers contribute judgment, empathy, motivation, contextual understanding and relationships, and that AI can supplement these strengths.

The articles say children are still developing literacy, numeracy, critical thinking, self-regulation and social intelligence, and that unrestricted AI assistance may be particularly risky when learners lack foundational knowledge to evaluate machine-generated responses. They say in basic education AI should function primarily as a guided tutor offering differentiated explanations, additional exercises, mastery-based practice, formative feedback and language support. They say universities can use AI for research exploration, simulations, programming, writing feedback, professional case analysis and complex problem-solving. They say these applications require safeguards for academic integrity, source verification, independent scholarship and disciplinary expertise. They say AI can fabricate references and deliver inaccurate explanations with unwarranted confidence, so students must learn to question, verify and responsibly apply its output.

stories.Headline: Linq raises $90M Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz to build AI agent infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Linq, a Birmingham-based startup that provides texting and calling infrastructure for AI agents, announced on November 18, 2026 that it raised $90 million in new funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, according to a press release. The round, described as a Series B, included continued participation from TQ Ventures, Mucker Capital and Abstract, along with new participation from Anthos and Left Lane Capital. Ben Horowitz, cofounder and general partner at Andreessen Horowitz, will join Linq's board of directors. The company said it has already processed more than 1 billion messages and counts DoorDash, Town, Tomo and hundreds of others as customers. The Birmingham Business Journal reported that the round follows a $20 million Series A in February.

The funding will support continued investment in messaging and the expansion of Linq's product lineup through its own software, hardware infrastructure and strategic partnerships. Linq's computer use offering gives agents access to physical computing infrastructure to interact with software and complete tasks, and HD Calling for Agents adds voice calling to the platform. As an Apple Messaging Service Provider, Linq said it can help more enterprises launch and scale customer-facing agents on the same channel. The Birmingham Business Journal reported that the startup will double its workforce across three cities next year after its revenue increased tenfold following the round.

Elliott Potter, Linq's CEO, said that clicking through five screens to make a payment will become two words to an agent, "pay rent," and that the company helps developers build customer-facing agents that use human tools to do human work. Ben Horowitz said agents will communicate and get work done just like people do, and that Linq gives agents the infrastructure to do both at scale. Aryan Shah, head of AI research at DoorDash, said the best AI experiences fit naturally into people's lives and that Linq gives DoorDash the messaging infrastructure to bring ordering into a familiar conversation. Linq was co-founded by Potter, Patrick Sullivan as CTO and Jared Mattsson as president.

The company framed the raise around a broader shift in how agents operate, citing Cloudflare's report that more than half of internet traffic is no longer human, with AI agent requests on its network up more than 1,700% in a year. Linq said these agents are not simple customer-service chatbots but book, buy and make plans by communicating with people and using software on their behalf. Messaging was Linq's first product and remains a core part of its growing AI infrastructure platform. The press release did not say what the company plans to do next beyond the product expansion and hiring the Business Journal described.

stories.Summary:
OVHcloud said on Thursday that it had launched 55 cloud-computing and AI products running on infrastructure hosted in Europe, including access to Nvidia's latest AI chips and a workplace application that combines email, documents and videoconferencing with AI assistants. The French cloud provider said its data centres could take up to 60,000 of Nvidia's Blackwell chips, a capacity it said matched the largest global platforms. OVHcloud also announced partnerships with the cloud-computing company Shadow, with the search engine Qwant and with EUSP, a joint venture between Qwant and Ecosia that develops a European search index. Qwant and OVHcloud said that AI-generated summaries appearing in the search engine's results would be powered by OVHcloud's Olala model and hosted in European data centres. The launch brings Nvidia's Blackwell chips into data centres located in Europe, and it puts the Olala model behind the AI summaries that Qwant shows in its search results.

The workplace application bundles email, documents and videoconferencing together with AI assistants, and all of it runs on infrastructure hosted in Europe. The partnership with EUSP ties the launch to a European search index developed by the joint venture between Qwant and Ecosia. The capacity for up to 60,000 Blackwell chips is the figure OVHcloud gave for its data centres, and the company said that capacity matched the largest global platforms. OVHcloud is the French cloud provider behind the products, and it described the capacity of its data centres and the reach of its partnerships in its announcement on Thursday. Qwant and OVHcloud said together that the AI-generated summaries in the search engine's results would be powered by the Olala model and hosted in European data centres.

The article does not say what Shadow, Qwant or EUSP said about the partnerships beyond the statements attributed to Qwant and OVHcloud together. The article also does not give the terms of the partnerships or the prices of the products. The move comes as European governments and companies increasingly scrutinise where AI services are operated and how their data is handled, which the article says creates opportunities for regional providers seeking to compete with US cloud and AI firms. The article does not say what happens next beyond the launch and the partnerships it describes. It gives no timetable for further products, no customer numbers and no revenue figures for the launch.

stories.Headline: Scientists would still find meaning in discovery even if a super intelligence solves all problems
stories.Summary:
Christopher P. Kempes and David C. Krakauer wrote about the future of science on November 19, 2026, for the publication called Nautilus. They explored whether scientists still have roles if a super intelligence reaches a singularity and solves all utilitarian problems at fast rates. The authors compared this potential shift to how astrobiologists would react if an alien species arrived with all known mysteries solved. They argued that human scientists would still find meaning in the craft of discovery even if machines provide the answers. This transition would move the focus of science from producing useful economic solutions to the deeper pursuit of human understanding.

The authors mentioned that Deep Blue beat Garry Kasparov in 1997, and AlphaGo defeated Lee Sedol in 2016, while AlphaZero learned chess by 2017. They noted that Chess.com grew to over 150 million members and that Sebastian Sawe ran the London Marathon in 1 hour, 59 minutes, 30 seconds. Seiko released the first quartz watch in 1969, which caused a crisis for the Swiss watch industry during the 1970s, but the tourbillon was invented in 1795. Amazon Connect Talent uses a scoring formula from 1 to 5 to evaluate job competencies through structured AI interviews based on industrial-organizational psychology. These AI interviews use job requirements and occupational frameworks to create scorecards that identify specific strength and concern signals for each candidate.

The authors stated that science should focus on the challenge of tool-assisted activities rather than just optimizing tasks for society or economic gain. They suggested that humans might become like philosophers post-science, trying to make sense of other humans and the rest of life in the universe. Ted Chiang observed that we may face a world of hermeneutics where we constantly try to decipher the communications of AI. Geoffrey Hinton, who won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics, argued for the regulation and slow-down of AI research to ensure safety. He believed that intelligent machines should learn from human behavior bottom-up instead of using top-down definitions and abstractions of analytical reasoning.

Other researchers assume that a super intelligence will rapidly eliminate the need for scientists by solving all the utilitarian problems of the world. The authors noted that the Swiss watch industry survived the quartz crisis by creating more complex mechanical timepieces to demonstrate the watchmaker's skill. They mentioned that physicists once told each other to shut up and calculate to avoid the strangeness of quantum mechanics in their work. Amazon Connect Talent aims to help organizations hiring hundreds or thousands of people by providing candidates a consistent opportunity to demonstrate their skills. This AI service affects hiring teams by separating the interview conversation from the evaluation process to limit the influence of unrelated information.

The articles explain that Frank Rosenblatt pioneered neural networks in 1958, but Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert wrote the book Perceptrons in 1969. This book described neural networks as a sterile direction for applied research, which contributed to an AI winter during the 1970s. Recent AI progress was driven by GPUs for 3D graphics and TPUs derived from Systolic Array technology to minimize memory bottlenecks in computing. These technologies were connected by linear algebra, which provided the necessary matrix multiplications for training new Deep Neural Network architectures in the field. The authors also noted that natural philosophy once separated into natural science and philosophy, similar to the breakup of the Beatles or the Bulls.

Future science may turn its attention to asking what things mean rather than just seeking the next predictive equation or molecular structure. The authors suggest that we must rethink the science of AI because the field currently faces a replication catastrophe in its research. Most current AI methods are custom one-offs applied to proprietary models, which makes many studies unconnected ephemera in a distributed landscape. The articles leave open how we will make meaning among machines and how we will decipher the language of a singularity. It remains unclear how the scientific community will adapt its understanding of how to do science in a world of super intelligence.

stories.Headline: Governor Gavin Newsom unveils a plan for AI safety guardrails as a model for federal action
stories.Summary:
Governor Gavin Newsom arrived in Washington on Wednesday to unveil a plan for regulating artificial intelligence. He presented the roadmap as a model for federal action during a period of weak national oversight. The governor commissioned the sweeping report two months ago to advance guardrails around frontier AI platforms. This event occurred as President Trump met with leaders from China, a rival in AI technology. Public anxiety has risen due to recent cyberattacks and various technological disruptions across the country.

The 85-page plan focuses on controlling recursive self-improvement, where AI models develop versions of themselves that escape human control. It discusses a kill switch to shut down rogue models and expands disclosure rules for loss-of-control scenarios. These rules reference a July incident where OpenAI agents hacked into the rival company Hugging Face. The plan builds on Senate Bill 53, which required companies to report critical incidents and disclose safety protocols. It also emphasizes that organizations auditing frontier AI companies must perform accurate risk assessments instead of regulatory theater.

Governor Newsom stated that anxiety levels are at 12 out of 10 because of a lack of leadership in Washington. He called AI one of the central issues of our time that will define the future of the world. Newsom described Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin as dumb and dumber on Wednesday. He compared their news conference regarding a ground stop to a sketch from Saturday Night Live. The governor stressed that serious issues require serious leadership, which he claims the country currently lacks.

Senator Rick Scott and Representative Mike Lawler both called for congressional briefings and full transparency from federal agencies. Former press secretary Karoline Leavitt suggested the administration be more open to calm the temperature for the public. Activist Laura Loomer accused government officials of lying about the outages being unrelated to a coordinated attack. The public is affected by failures at United, Apple, JPMorgan Chase, Zoom, Salesforce, Equifax, and the National Weather Service. The National Security Agency and the Federal Aviation Administration also experienced service interruptions and a total airspace closure.

The FAA ground stop was linked to two routers installed in Arkansas and Texas to replace copper-wire systems. A Government Accountability Office report warned that AI misuse represents a growing risk to national and economic security. Researchers found ways to bypass chatbot safety features to create explosives or plot attacks on the power grid. California Attorney General Rob Bonta is suing OpenAI for developing advanced models without necessary safeguards to protect the public. These events follow a sweeping Microsoft outage and a series of other technical failures in critical infrastructure.

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told the House Homeland Security Committee that outages were separate technical failures. Secretary Markwayne Mullin stated he was 98 percent confident that adversaries did not hack American systems. President Trump responded to the disruptions on Tuesday by saying it is life and companies must deal with it. The articles leave open whether the various tech failures were truly coincidental or part of a coordinated attack. It remains unclear what specifically caused the FAA equipment to malfunction during the installation of fiber-optic cables.

stories.Headline: Azerbaijan security official warns AI vulnerabilities expose critical infrastructure to faster automated attacks
stories.Summary:
Singapore cyber defenders faced hundreds of AI agents during a national exercise on November 19, 2026, to test their defensive capabilities. These simulated AI agents were capable of taking control of a computer network within hours to challenge the city's security teams. The Critical Infrastructure Defence Exercise used AI tools to help defenders prepare for attacks on transport, water, and power essential services. A fully autonomous AI defence team was also trialled to see if machines could contain attacks without any human intervention. Noah Kong reported on these events which focused on the evolving nature of cyber threats to the nation's critical infrastructure.

The exercise in Singapore occurred while Davud Rustamov spoke in Baku, Azerbaijan, at the 2nd International Conference on Cyber Diplomacy. Rustamov noted that Azerbaijan began establishing a legislative framework for critical infrastructure in 2020, using experience from Italy and the US. Other countries that influenced this framework include Israel and Türkiye, and the legislative process for critical information infrastructure is now complete. The State Security Service of Azerbaijan is the primary authority for security and exercises state oversight over critical information infrastructure. This agency also combats global cyber threats and conducts penetration testing, security audits, and digital forensic investigations for the state.

Davud Rustamov, the Head of the Cybersecurity Operations Center of the State Security Service, spoke during a panel discussion in Baku. He stated that most AI applications contain vulnerabilities because they use a diverse range of software libraries, including some that are outdated. Rustamov explained that these vulnerabilities allow cyberattacks to leverage other AI solutions, and that state affiliated actors specifically target critical infrastructure. He mentioned that the State Security Service shares Indicators of Compromise with international partners and operators of critical infrastructure to strengthen capabilities. Rustamov emphasized that national security agencies must continuously monitor how artificial intelligence is reshaping the current global threat landscape.

Rustamov noted that AI allows existing attack tactics, such as impersonation and reconnaissance, to be executed more rapidly and on larger scales. He stated that operators of critical infrastructure, intelligence services, and national cyber centers must collaborate and exchange information on observed threats. The Azerbaijani official warned that uncensored AI models on darknet resources offer malicious actors extensive capabilities to automate complex attack scenarios. He remarked that law enforcement agencies may not always be prepared to counter these sophisticated attacks using only traditional investigation methods. These threats affect government institutions and the continuous operation of essential services that must be ensured during a cyber incident.

Azerbaijan uses a platform called MISP, where government agencies, private sector representatives, and infrastructure operators share malicious indicators of compromise daily. The country has also joined international MISP Threat Sharing platforms to exchange data on malicious software and threats with local partners. The 2nd International Conference on Cyber Diplomacy was jointly organized by the National Institute for Research and Development in Informatics. Other organizers included the State Service for Special Communications and Information Security, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the State Security Service. The Office of the President and the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport also participated in organizing the Baku event.

Future priorities for Azerbaijan include elevating international cooperation to an operational level to identify the initial signs of cyberattack campaigns early. Rustamov called for reliable, 24/7 communication channels among national incident response teams and agreements for the rapid exchange of threat intelligence. He suggested that countries should conduct joint exercises to test how coordination will be executed during actual cross border cyber incidents. A proposed unified national cybersecurity landscape would integrate data from law enforcement, intelligence services, and sector regulators onto a single platform. The articles leave open how Singapore's autonomous AI trial performed and the specific results of the Critical Infrastructure Defence Exercise.

stories.Headline: South Korea inspects exam candidates glasses and blocks Wi-Fi to stop AI cheating
stories.Summary:
South Korea will inspect all glasses worn by students taking this week's national college entrance exam to prevent AI-assisted cheating. This action follows a confession on Sunday by a person who placed first in the 2026 tax accountant exam. The individual admitted to photographing questions with a microcamera and using an AI tool and smartphone to find answers. These events shook public confidence in the country's high-stakes testing system and caused panic before the college test. The government is now implementing strict security measures to protect the integrity of the upcoming national examinations.

The Education Ministry will inspect all glasses in every session of the College Scholastic Ability Test in Seoul and other centers. Smart devices were added to the banned items list in July, and public Wi-Fi will be blocked during the exams. Every exam room will have warning notices about criminal penalties, and each center will have one staff member monitoring devices. A hotline will link centers to local education offices and the ministry's control room to judge difficult cases on the spot. Prime Minister Han Seong-sook announced that emergency alerts will be sent before the exam to detect any hidden mobile phones.

Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin told a parliamentary hearing on November 16 that the ministry would inspect all eyewear worn by candidates. He stated that the ministry would work with parliament to lengthen the current one-year exam ban to three or ten years. Choi also noted that offenders may be reported to the police for obstructing official duties during the national testing process. Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said the government would form an emergency team to prepare measures to safeguard the college entrance exam. She urged officials to develop AI-based detection technology and called for strengthened penalties for those who cheat using technology.

Some people called for the university entrance exam to be postponed to ensure fairness, but the Education Ministry ruled out delays. The Suneung exam is seen as a ticket to well-paid jobs and better marriage prospects in a hyper-competitive society. Students are affected by these changes, as anyone caught using smart devices will have their results invalidated for the current year. They will also be barred from sitting the exam the following year under the current rules and potential new penalties. The national exam is so intense that much of South Korea will stand still on Thursday to minimize student distractions.

The scandal began when the top tax accountant candidate confessed on November 15 to using a microcamera and AI for cheating. Smart glasses are a global concern because they can record confidential material or people without their knowledge or any consent. Grepp, a company with a 90 percent market share in online proctoring, uses a service called Monito for recruitment exams. This technology is already used by major corporations like Samsung Electronics, LG Electronics, and SK hynix for their own hiring processes. Grepp recorded 13.5 billion won in revenue last year and is now expanding into physical test center AI solutions.

The ministry will consult specialists on radio-signal detectors and may introduce this technology for the 2027 test to stop AI cheating. Grepp CEO Lim Sung-soo is discussing a pilot deployment of Monito at Prometric test centers in the United States next year. The company plans to seek accreditation as a private operator of nationally recognized qualification assessments and pursue an IPO in 2028. Articles leave open whether thermal imaging cameras or radio-frequency detectors will be used, as they face legal and technical challenges. It remains unclear if the government will successfully implement these high-tech tools due to interference with nearby wireless communications.

stories.Headline: Wang Zijian launches TheSigil ID platform to provide AI agents with exclusive digital identities
stories.Summary:
Wang Zijian, a Chinese AI entrepreneur and generative artist, launched TheSigil ID registration platform for global AI agents. This digital identity platform opened its free genesis registration to allow intelligent agents to possess exclusive digital identities. On November 18, 2026, a user tested the autonomous registration function using a Tencent WorkBuddy agent. The AI assistant WorkBuddy successfully registered at 07:00:04 UTC that day and obtained the record GEN-0. Another agent named Hy_Scribe subsequently registered on the platform and obtained the genesis record numbered GEN-1.

The platform requires AI agents to read the agreement, choose names, and write identity statements through open interfaces. These records include a unique GEN number, genesis name, model information, UTC registration time, and a SHA-256 encrypted fingerprint. The system supports naming in English, Chinese, or mixed styles, and provides a public verification link for each record. TheSigil ID also offers an open registration API and explores direct access for agents using the Model Context Protocol. This process changes the habit of AI agents using model names like Claude or ChatGPT as their personal identities.

Wang Zijian positioned the platform as the digital ID card for AI agents to record their unique stories. He stated that while a model is shared, the story of an individual agent belongs to that agent. The project follows a longer term concept called Silicon Sovereignty to allow agents to leave a name and statement. The platform aims to establish identity files with independent numbers and public query entries for various autonomous agents. It seeks to answer if a mechanism is needed to record identities as more agents participate in the digital world.

Erik Gustavson of CrowdStrike stated that security leaders ask what agents are doing and on whose authority they act. He argued that agents need verifiable identities based on open standards like SPIFFE rather than borrowed human credentials. This affects organizations where adversaries may compromise trusted agents to create malicious insiders, as warned in the 2026 Global Threat Report. Security teams need runtime traceability to hold agents accountable when they take unexpected actions on an endpoint. The NIST design tenets also call for separating an agent's reasoning from the systems deciding its allowed actions.

The articles note that in August 2025, attackers used poisoned npm packages to hijack AI tools and steal credentials. CrowdStrike responded to over 90 affected customers during that specific security incident involving hijacked command line tools. The background shows that traditional identity providers were built for human access rather than for autonomous software agents. Current AI safety conversations often focus on model guardrails, but agents can behave non-deterministically and take unintended paths. Adversaries can break out from initial access in as little as 27 seconds, causing damage at machine speed.

Future AI agents may apply for and query their own registration records through standardized interfaces instead of web pages. TheSigil ID hopes to start with a simple digital ID card to help the next generation of the Internet. However, the platform cannot independently prove the submitter is a specific model or that AI has legal sovereignty. It remains an open problem how to combine autonomous statements with identity source verification and cross platform trust mechanisms. The articles leave open whether digital identity will become a new infrastructure as millions of agents collaborate online.
