stories.Headline: Anthropic raises a record $813 billion in its Nasdaq IPO and closes up 17%
stories.Summary:
Anthropic debuted on the Nasdaq on November 19, 2026, under the ticker ANT, with a final IPO price of $83 per share. The stock opened at $111.50 and surged to an intraday peak of $115.10. On a fully diluted basis its market capitalization once reached approximately $2.08 trillion. Based on issued shares the figure was around $1.51 trillion. It closed at $97.17, roughly 17% higher than the IPO price at market close.

Its fundraising amount hit $813 billion, surpassing SpaceX and setting a new global IPO fundraising record. At its intraday peak Anthropic became the sixth largest listed company by market cap globally on a fully diluted basis. It ranked after Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet and Amazon. As of September 30, 2026, it had approximately 5,300 employees. At the peak intraday market cap, each employee created a market cap of $392.5 million, roughly 4.7 times that of Nvidia.

According to the prospectus, revenue generated per capita in the past 12 months exceeded $6.6 million. Calculated at the peak intraday stock price, the total net worth of its seven co-founders exceeded $190 billion. In October, investors were still discussing that Anthropic's listing valuation could reach around $2 trillion. As the listing approached, market discussions fell back to the $1.2 trillion to $1.4 trillion range. By the time of its listing, the market cap surged back to $2 trillion.

The three major US stock indexes all closed lower on the day. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 2.19%, the S&P 500 Index dropped 2.02%, and the Nasdaq Composite Index declined 2.25%. After the US midterm elections, the Democratic Party will gain a majority in Congress next January. Recent policy discussions within the party have placed more emphasis on strengthening accountability for AI companies. They also stress protecting workers and consumers and paying attention to the impact of data centers on power supply, the environment and local communities.

Anthropic's earliest publicly disclosed financing was its 2021 Series A round, led by Jaan Tallinn, Skype co-founder and investor, raising $124 million. The 2025 Series E and Series F rounds raised approximately $35 billion and $130 billion respectively. The 2026 Series G and Series H rounds raised $300 billion and approximately $650 billion respectively. After the Series H round, the company's disclosed post-money valuation reached $965 billion.

According to OECD statistics, AI companies received approximately $258.7 billion in venture capital in 2025, accounting for 61% of total global venture capital, twice the proportion in 2022. In the first half of 2026, according to WIPO statistics, the proportion of AI financing in global venture capital rose to 77%, with OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI alone accounting for nearly 43%. Before its IPO, Amazon invested approximately $18 billion through convertible bonds and preferred shares. Among the Magnificent Seven, four companies have investment and cooperative supply chain relationships with Anthropic: Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Nvidia.

The proportion of revenue generated by purchasing Claude through cloud service providers' marketplace rose from 11% in 2023 to 47% in 2025, and stood at around 44% in the first nine months of 2026. According to Anthropic's latest prospectus released on November 10, seven companies including Google, Nvidia and Microsoft agreed to collectively purchase $26 billion of non-voting Class N shares at the IPO price concurrently with the IPO. In the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Anthropic's revenue was $33.242 billion. Usage-based revenue was $26.306 billion, about 79%, and subscription revenue was $6.936 billion, about 21%.

Customers who spent more than $100,000 in the past 12 months contributed about 74% of revenue in the past 9 months, and their number exceeded 11,900. In the nine months ended September 2026, Anthropic recorded an operating loss of approximately $1.26 billion and a net loss of approximately $104.039 billion. Approximately $94.324 billion of the net loss came from fair value changes of items such as convertible bonds, derivatives and SAFE, and operating cash flow was positive at approximately $6.6 billion. Computing power and infrastructure expenses in the first nine months of 2026 were approximately $18.8 billion, about 57% of revenue in the same period, and the company said this expense is expected to remain its largest operating expense for the foreseeable future.

stories.Headline: The Challenger Team develops an AI intelligent CNC grinding machine to reduce reliance on foreign imports
stories.Summary:
The Challenger Team, a high-end equipment group founded in March 2024, developed a full hydrostatic ultra-precision AI intelligent CNC grinding machine to break overseas monopolies. This effort aims to achieve independent controllability over industrial mother machines that are critical for high-end manufacturing in China. The team focused on tackling core technologies to overcome targeted embargoes and restrictions imposed by giants from Japan, Germany, and Switzerland. These ultra-precision grinders are essential for producing components with sub-micron and nano-level precision for the aerospace and semiconductor sectors.

The project requires the integration of an ultra-precision hydrostatic spindle with a radial runout of 0.2μm and an axial play of 0.1μm. It utilizes the Huazhong AI intelligent CNC system from Huazhong University of Science and Technology to provide automatic programming and precision deviation compensation. This technology addresses the failure of domestic bearings to meet P2 grade precision and reduces the 92 percent import share of high-end bearings. The development follows the thin-film feedback hydrostatic route pioneered by Academician Zhou Qinzhi to ensure consistent machining precision.

Guan Shihe spent over 20 years developing the critical hydrostatic spindle to match the precision of European brands like STUDER and Hover. Professor Dai Huiliang, a successor to Academician Zhou, stated that the team is fulfilling the academician's wish to industrialize domestic mirror grinding technology. The team noted that a current lack of funds limits them to selling spindles and hydraulic systems to help bearing manufacturers upgrade. They believe that these advancements will finally remove the bottlenecks hindering the production of precision ball screws and machine tool spindles.

This initiative aligns with the Outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan, which identifies industrial mother machines as a strategically critical field. The government intends to use the national Industrial Mother Machine Special Fund and other fiscal policies to support these decisive technological breakthroughs. Future efforts will focus on developing integrated compound high-end CNC machine tools to enhance national security and industrial upgrading. The current policy environment provides a foundation for the future development of high-precision and ultra-precision industrial mother machines.

stories.Headline: Chinese tech giants prioritize AI infrastructure spending over immediate profits
stories.Summary:
Chinese tech giants increased AI infrastructure spending during 2026, which shifted their cash flow from profit amplification to capital financing. Tencent, Alibaba, and Baidu all reported significant capital expenditures that reduced their free cash flow during the third quarter. Tencent saw its share price fall nearly 6 percent to HK$350.4 on November 19 after releasing financial results. This sell-off followed a report showing net cash from operating activities dropped to RMB 2.6 billion from RMB 85.3 billion. The companies are prioritizing the procurement of computing power and GPUs over immediate profits to remain competitive in the market.

Tencent spent RMB 81.4 billion in the third quarter, including an RMB 86 billion advance payment for computing power. This payment supports the Hunyuan Model and WorkBuddy, while long-term assets rose from RMB 24.5 billion to RMB 162.9 billion. Alibaba spent RMB 50.477 billion in the third quarter, contributing to a free cash flow outflow of RMB 34.472 billion. Alibaba's three-year RMB 3800 billion plan, announced in February 2025, had invested RMB 1900 billion by June 2026. Baidu reported a quarterly capital expenditure of RMB 7.35 billion and a free cash flow gap of -RMB 4.57 billion.

Tencent CFO Lo Siu Hon stated that advance payments were necessary to lock in GPUs for model upgrades and inference. President Martin Lau compared these investments to building a factory that can produce continuously and train future models. Alibaba CFO Xu Hong focused on improving return on invested capital and aiming for positive free cash flow soon. Baidu management explained that existing production capacity and self-developed Kunlun Core M100 chips help meet their incremental demand. James Mitchell of Tencent noted that investment levels have peaked and will remain steady through 2027.

Investors are concerned whether AI can bring measurable revenue growth through advertising, transaction conversion, or cloud services, according to Catherine Lim. Morgan Stanley cut the target price for Tencent by nearly 13 percent to HK$480 due to these cash flow concerns. ByteDance is affected by these trends, having signed a US$29.6 billion syndicated loan to secure data center capacity. Alibaba shareholders were impacted by a HK$80 billion rights issue in August to expand global computing and AI facilities. These companies are now using debt instruments and rights issues rather than relying on steady free cash flow.

Historically, Chinese internet platforms maintained light assets and high cash flow conversion rates to support large share repurchases. Bloomberg estimates that domestic internet company capital expenditure in 2026 will reach US$66 billion, a 77 percent increase from 2025. Morgan Stanley reports that Chinese server capital expenditure is three times higher than in the United States, with lower recovery efficiency. The return on invested capital for Chinese cloud vendors is 13 percent, compared to 31 percent for American vendors. Tencent's balance sheet shifted from net cash of RMB 58.2 billion to net debt of RMB 13.7 billion.

Tencent expects a financial turning point in 2028, while James Mitchell suggests improvements will come in that same year. Goldman Sachs expects Alibaba to face a funding gap through fiscal 2028, reaching capital balance by fiscal 2029. Alibaba Cloud reported Q3 revenue of RMB 60.973 billion, showing that revenue growth is accelerating despite the cash outflows. The articles leave open whether the revenue growth from these assets will eventually exceed the rising depreciation costs. It remains uncertain if these massive investments will translate into the measurable profits that cautious market investors demand.

stories.Headline: Melania Trump launches AI competition for K-12 students and schools
stories.Summary:
Melania Trump is pushing a new education initiative that encourages artificial intelligence for expanding knowledge. She made this a priority for children and educators at the start of Donald Trump's second term. The White House announced the 2027 Presidential Super Intelligence Challenge for K-12 students and schools in October. This team based competition asks students to create innovations to address pressing challenges in their communities. Participating schools can earn the First Lady Seal of SI Readiness by completing specific milestones.

Schools can sign up by December 18 and complete milestones by April 30, 2027. A 2025 executive order made AI literacy a federal policy to maintain competitiveness in the global economy. President Trump issued an order on September 29 requiring agencies to use the term super intelligence. This term refers to systems defined in section 9401(3) of title 15, United States Code. The Department of Education issued guidance for schools to receive federal funding for these AI initiatives.

Melania Trump said AI extends the conceptual and that curiosity opens doors to innovation and leadership. She stated that only humans generate meaning and purpose through deep thinking, patience, and staying curious. In March, she suggested a humanoid robot named Plato could serve as a personalized educator in homes. She believes the private and public sectors must work together for real growth in technology and education. Trump also noted that users must be vigilant and not believe everything AI agents share with them.

Tracy Weeks of Instructure supports encouraging students and educators to become more comfortable with AI tools. She noted that districts must balance innovation with concerns about screen time and keeping children safe. Matt Maher of M7 Innovations fears the intellect of the next generation will be collateral damage. He believes the initiative lacks specifics and focuses more on winning an AI arms race than empowerment. Maher stated that parents must self regulate if the government and developers do not provide proper rules.

Melania Trump has focused on children since first entering the White House in 2017 through various campaigns. Her previous efforts included housing vouchers, savings accounts, anti bullying campaigns, and helping children in war zones. The administration aims to maintain U.S. leadership in AI development, particularly in competition with China. The current executive order claims today's frontier systems amplify human ingenuity across science and medicine. The first lady also leads a Fostering the Future Global Coalition with other first ladies.

Winners of the Super Intelligence competition will be invited to the White House to receive an award. Melania Trump is focusing on initiatives to complete in the next two years, including women's health innovation. Her global coalition has held gatherings in Miami, the Philippines, Poland, and St. Kitts and Nevis. The articles do not state the specific milestones schools must complete for the readiness seal. They also leave open how the government will provide the suggested humanoid robot educators to homes.

stories.Headline: AINU AI launches a creation platform to standardize short video production for e-commerce marketing
stories.Summary:
AINU AI launched a one-stop creation platform in September 2026 to standardize short video production for e-commerce marketing. The company aims to transform viral hit videos into a standardized production pipeline for creators and merchants. This platform integrates the entire workflow from topic selection and script writing to generation and final production. It focuses on the earlier parts of the workflow rather than just providing an entry for generation models. The system allows users to discover, iterate, and create high-quality viral videos within a single interface.

The platform includes a Global Viral Data Dashboard that aggregates real-time popular videos from TikTok, Douyin, and Xiaohongshu. It uses data from TikTok influencers like ash tervino vs bri, Douyin food accounts, and Xiaohongshu nail art categories. The Script Master tool generates scripts and storyboards, offering eight built-in official preset skills like Douyin voiceover. Video generation is powered by multiple models, including Wan 3.0, Seedance 2.0, and Seedance 2.5, for various scenarios. Specialized modules provide clothing detail images, product selling point images, and both instrumental and lyric music creation.

The AINU AI team consists of nearly 100 members who independently control core research, model iteration, and computing power. They stated that the platform is designed by reversely deducing functions from the needs of e-commerce sellers. The company believes the next stage of competition lies in connecting the whole process from start to finish. By betting on the workflow, they aim to enable one person to complete work that previously required three people. They rely on a self-built computing power server room to support their large-scale delivery of content.

The platform serves 540,000 merchants and 2.2 million influencers, reaching a total accumulated content play volume over 500 million. E-commerce practitioners, individual merchants, and small teams are the primary groups affected by this assembly line approach. These users prioritize producing useful videos quickly over finding the single best model available on the market. The platform provides inspiration templates for catering, entertainment, daily life convenience, store materials, tourism, and domestic services. It also features AINU TV, a community where users publish works and create secondary content.

The company has an annual AI content production capacity of nearly 2 million hours to support its operations. AINU AI differentiates itself from Kling, Jimeng, and Runway by focusing on the full workflow rather than single-point model capabilities. While Kling focuses on character movement and Jimeng integrates with Jianying, Runway targets professional film and television post-production. AINU AI uses a Knowledge Base Brain to train exclusive AI brains using uploaded product manuals and brand documents. The Viral Content Replication function analyzes shot structures and prompt logic to disassemble the ideas of viral content.

The company must now navigate a crowded market where model manufacturers and editing software developers are both expanding. A significant challenge is that model aggregation leaves the platform restricted by the authorization and pricing of upstream suppliers. It is also difficult for a full-process platform to achieve industry-leading performance in every single individual link. Professional creators may still prefer single-point depth over the broad coverage offered by this integrated e-commerce tool. The articles leave open how the company will adjust its strategy if upstream model providers tighten their access.

stories.Headline: Hong Kong stocks drop toward 19-month low as AI investment doubts rattle investors
stories.Summary:
Hong Kong stocks declined on Friday, November 20, 2026, pushing the benchmark gauge toward a nearly 19-month low. This downturn occurred as the debut of the AI frontier lab Anthropic in the United States failed to restore investor confidence. Market participants remained rattled by doubts regarding whether massive investments in data centers could produce comparable financial returns. These persistent jitters surrounding artificial intelligence technology contributed to a tumultuous week of swings for various stocks.

The Hang Seng Index dropped 1.9 per cent to 22,410.80, marking its lowest closing point since April 30 of the previous year. Simultaneously, the Hang Seng Tech Index slid 3.8 per cent while the chip-centric Star 50 gauge slumped 3.1 per cent. On the Chinese mainland, the CSI 300 Index sank 0.8 per cent during the same trading period. Tencent Holdings fell to its lowest level in over two years after quarterly results revealed that AI expenditures reduced earnings and eroded cash flow.

The decline in these indices complicated ongoing government efforts to establish a floor under the stocks on the Chinese mainland. The situation was exacerbated by external shocks that weighed heavily on the technology sector and broader market sentiment. Investors are now closely monitoring whether the high costs of developing artificial intelligence will eventually be offset by significant profits. No further details regarding future government interventions or specific recovery timelines were provided in the reports.

stories.Headline: Chinese investors shift capital to consumer stocks amid AI sector volatility
stories.Summary:
Investors in China began shifting their capital into beaten-down consumer stocks during November 2026 to avoid the volatility of artificial intelligence trading. This movement occurred as a significant sell-off of technology stocks created turmoil across the mainland exchanges. Many traders viewed these consumer assets as safe havens because their prices had languished during the broader economic slowdown. The shift reflects a desire to find stability while the high-growth tech sector experienced a sharp decline. The CSI index of consumer stocks rose nearly 5 per cent this month after previously gaining 2.9 per cent in October.

Meanwhile, the Star 50 index which tracks the largest AI chipmakers in China has slumped more than 40 per cent since its record high in June. This divergence shows a clear rotation of funds away from expensive technology firms toward undervalued consumer companies. These changes highlight the extreme volatility currently affecting the artificial intelligence sector compared to traditional consumer markets. The China Securities Regulatory Commission addressed the situation on Wednesday by denying online rumours about administrative interference in mutual-fund investments.

The regulator stated that it had not required fund firms to report their specific exposures to the artificial intelligence sector. According to the commission, money managers have made their own independent investment decisions while following fund mandates and relevant laws. This official statement aimed to calm the market after reports suggested the government was influencing portfolio allocations. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Anthropic IPO fails to reverse slump in artificial intelligence investments
stories.Summary:
Asian shares declined on Friday, November 20, 2026, as the public debut of Anthropic failed to reverse a broader slump in artificial intelligence investments. The Hang Seng Index in Hong Kong opened down 359 points, or 1.57 percent, at 22,482, while the China enterprises index dropped 122 points, or 1.59 percent, to 7,568. The Hong Kong tech index dived 107 points, or 2.95 percent, to 3,541, and the Shanghai Composite Index opened down 50 points, or 1.41 percent, at 3,527. On the mainland, the Shenzhen Component Index lost 180 points, or 1.71 percent, to open at 10,402, and the ChiNext Index fell 49 points, or 2.15 percent, to 2,244.

These losses followed a decline of more than two percent for both the Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500 in the United States. Although shares of Anthropic surged more than 30 percent during its historic debut as the first publicly traded frontier AI company, the move did not restore general investor faith. The market remains pressured by a rallying US dollar and the fact that Asian shares are on track for their worst week since 2020. This volatility reflects a wider struggle to maintain the momentum of AI trades across global equity markets.

Kyle Rodda, a senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, stated that the successful IPO was not enough to ease concerns about the AI trade and general equities. He noted that market sentiment is currently shaky because the AI trade is fading and Federal Reserve rate hikes appear likely. Rodda warned that this prevailing bearishness carries the risk of dragging stock prices even lower in the near future. His analysis suggests that the initial excitement surrounding new AI listings cannot outweigh the broader economic anxieties currently facing investors.

The AI sector has been further weakened by the departure of Jensen Huang as the CEO of Nvidia and growing opposition to data centers following the Democratic sweep of US midterm elections. Additional negative pressure comes from warnings that artificial intelligence could threaten human extinction and concerns regarding mounting debt loads within the industry. These combined factors have bruised investor sentiment and created a difficult environment for technology stocks. The market now faces a period of instability as it balances technological potential against significant political and financial risks.

stories.Headline: Workers AI Superintelligence team releases open-weight Clairic and Clairic-flash models
stories.Summary:
The Workers AI Superintelligence team released updated versions of Clairic and Clairic-flash on November 18, 2026. These two models are now available as open-weight options for users. Cloudflare created these frontier AI models for its customers and the open-source community. The team redesigned the architecture of Clairic after its initial preview release. This update focuses on improving how the model handles unstructured data.

The new Clairic improves extraction from PDFs, images, tables, lists, and dates. Clairic-flash is a compact model with 9 billion parameters for faster performance. Both models are hosted on Workers AI and available on Hugging Face. The updated Clairic uses parallel slot autoregressive generation for text and number fields. This replaces the single forward pass used in the previous preview version.

Alex Reneau, Michelle Chen, and Kevin Flansburg represent the Workers AI Superintelligence team. They stated that Cloudflare has become a neolab for building frontier AI models. The team is working quickly to push the AI frontier for the community. They explained that the redesign makes extraction the clear focus for the model. This allows the model to excel at reading from unstructured data sources.

Customers provided feedback and use cases that influenced the redesign of the model. These users wanted to extract data from support tickets and images like receipts. The open-source community is also affected by the release of these open weights. These groups needed more reliable grounding of answers in the source material. The updates specifically address these needs for better data extraction and prediction.

The team previously announced a preview version of the Clairic extraction model. They also developed another model called Clef before this current release. The company has been building a research team to create useful AI models. This background led to the creation of the Workers AI Superintelligence team. They used customer feedback to go back to the drawing board for Clairic.

The team is currently working on many more models for future release. These new models will continue to serve Cloudflare customers and open-source developers. The articles do not state when the next model will be released. They do not specify the exact size of the full Clairic model. It remains open whether further architectural changes will be made to Clairic-flash.

stories.Headline: Veteran broker Allen Buchanan says curiosity trumps age in learning AI
stories.Summary:
Allen C. Buchanan, a commercial real estate broker with Lee & Associates in Orange, wrote in a column published by the Orange County Register on November 21, 2026, that he once feared he was too old to learn artificial intelligence. He recalled that a remarkable tool began filtering into everyday life at the end of 2022, and that by mid-2023 the technology was off to the races. His first reaction, he wrote, was that he was too freaking old to learn something new, even though he had created an online voice in 2009 that led to his column. He nevertheless took small steps, learning about ChatGPT prompts and the like, and nearly four years later he set out what he had learned.

Buchanan wrote that a person does not have to understand how something works to benefit from it, comparing AI to driving a car without being able to explain its engine. He said curiosity trumps age, noting that since he began brokering commercial real estate in 1984 he had seen fax machines, personal computers, email, the internet, smartphones and social media each change how business was done. He advised that the better the question, the better the answer, because explaining who you are, what you want to accomplish, the audience and the desired outcome improves results dramatically. He added that experience still matters, since AI can analyze a lease, compare buildings, research a company or suggest a negotiating strategy, but technology provides information while experience supplies judgment.

Buchanan described how his use grew from an occasional question to creating applications, developing training programs and analyzing complicated real estate transactions, while calling himself simply a curious old broker rather than a technology expert. He said imagination may be the greatest limitation, asking what about the things people never attempted because they were too complicated, time-consuming or expensive. He cautioned that AI makes mistakes, occasionally spectacular ones, and can confidently provide information that is completely wrong, so human oversight remains essential, especially when advising clients on decisions involving millions of dollars. His advice to those still sitting on the sidelines was to buy a ticket, because the journey is just beginning.

Articles.Title: Afraid of AI? You’re never too old to learn something new

stories.Headline: Professor Feigh says checking AI outputs erases the productivity gains generative AI promises
stories.Summary:
Karen Feigh, a professor of cognitive engineering at the Georgia Institute of Technology, wrote in the Conversation that the productivity gains from generative AI are being offset by the large amount of time and effort needed to clean up its outputs, according to a Futurism article published on November 21, 2026. She pointed in particular to a phenomenon known as the verification burden, a machine learning concept that refers to the wasted time humans spend checking the accuracy of the technology's work. Feigh explained that at a deeper level the burden is the cognitive cost of trying to regain authority over work that is partly delegated to a system while the worker keeps responsibility for the final product. The article says the phenomenon probably explains the findings of a recent Stanford survey, which found that most workers forced to use AI on the job are really just churning out low-effort busywork.

That busywork, which the article calls workslop, gives the appearance of passable reports and memos but inevitably demands more effort from employees down the line. A separate analysis found that workers who do try to check their AI work before sending it on end up wasting more of their own time doing so, especially compared with employees who do not touch AI at all. Feigh wrote that workplace verification tasks are fundamentally different from the act of creating things ourselves, because drafting a pitch deck generally comes with an obvious end point while double-checking an AI-drafted pitch deck is a whole different beast. She explained that a worker generally knows when something they are creating is done or at least sufficient for the task, but when to stop verification is less obvious.

Feigh said a worker must decide what to check and how, without knowing whether an error exists, where it might be or what form it might take. The article concludes that, put together, it is no wonder AI has not revolutionized labor, because it is simply much more trouble than it is worth. The piece links to related coverage saying companies are realizing they are spending a fortune on AI just so their employees can generate error-riddled slop, and are suddenly cutting back budgets. It also links to Stanford research finding that companies are being torn apart by AI workslop, and to a study finding that AI use at work is causing brain fry, especially among high performers.

Articles.Title: AI Is Still So Riddled With Errors That It's Erasing Any Productivity Gains That Would Make It Useful in the Workplace

stories.Headline: Nscale suspends hiring across several divisions to cut costs ahead of a potential $35bn flotation
stories.Summary:
The British artificial intelligence company Nscale halted recruitment in several divisions on November 21, 2026, to reduce costs. This decision follows a period of rapid growth and comes as the firm prepares for a potential $35bn flotation on the New York Stock Exchange. The company has seen its workforce expand from 300 employees earlier this year to more than 1,100 people. This move occurs amid a broader market sell-off and rising borrowing costs for data centre operators.

The cost-cutting drive requires executives to suspend hiring for a few months, except for critical roles, and reduce discretionary spending. Nscale, which was founded two years ago by former cryptocurrency executive Josh Payne, has raised over $13bn and signed deals with Microsoft and Anthropic. The company reported a loss of $1.7bn during the first nine months of this year on revenues of $308m. Additionally, Nscale lost a $3.2bn Microsoft deal due to delays in securing a grid connection.

Chief operating officer Justin Osofsky, who previously worked at Meta, told staff that the business needs time to catch up with its growth. He explained that financing large projects is taking longer across the sector, making careful cash management essential for future opportunities. Osofsky stated that preserving every dollar provides the company with more flexibility to fund its highest priority projects. He emphasized that the firm must hold itself to a higher bar regarding its spending.

The company faces a difficult environment following the departure of Nvidia boss Jensen Huang and anti-data centre victories in the US Midterms. Nscale also warned Norwegian officials that its expansion plans could fall apart due to a moratorium on new data centres. In a letter dated November 1, the firm requested an urgent meeting with Norway's energy ministry. Ministers subsequently blocked new grid connections and technical approvals for data centres until next August.

Articles.Title: British AI giant Nscale halts hiring in cost-cutting drive - The Telegraph

stories.headline_source: British AI giant Nscale halts hiring in cost-cutting drive

stories.Headline: Singapore and China pledge to deepen cooperation in artificial intelligence
stories.Summary:
Singapore and China launched talks to upgrade their bilateral free trade agreement on Friday, November 20, 2026. Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and President Xi Jinping met at Kylin Villa in Shenzhen to discuss these ties. The leaders pledged to deepen relations between the two countries amid current global shake-ups. They also discussed how to deepen cooperation in emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence. This meeting was the third between the two leaders since Wong took office in May 2024.

The upgrade, called China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement 4.0, requires a memorandum of understanding between METI and China's Ministry of Commerce. It will cover the digital economy and government procurement to open new markets for Singapore companies. The agreement will facilitate cross-border data flows and build on the 2009 original bilateral free trade agreement. It also leverages the Suzhou Industrial Park, Sino-Singapore Tianjin Eco-City, and the Chongqing Connectivity Initiative. These efforts follow the 2023 upgrade to an All-Round High-Quality Future-Oriented Partnership.

Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said the partnership has expanded into connectivity and green development despite a complex international environment. He noted that both nations can learn from each other to help businesses innovate and raise productivity. President Xi Jinping stated that cooperation over the past few years has brought tangible benefits to both peoples. He described the two nations as friendly neighbours and key development partners during the meeting. Xi called for closer strategic communication to take the partnership to new heights.

President Xi noted that the world is undergoing profound changes with a new round of technological revolution. Prime Minister Wong urged Apec leaders to prevent the Asia-Pacific from splitting into competing economic blocs. He stated that dialogue is valuable for peace and stability during a time of heightened geopolitical tensions. Singapore companies are affected as the upgrade aims to make it easier for them to do business. Workers are also affected as the leaders discussed preparing them for future jobs.

China was Singapore's largest merchandise trading partner from 2013 to 2024 and its third-largest services partner in 2024. Bilateral merchandise trade totalled S$162.9 billion in 2025, which was 11.7 per cent of Singapore's global merchandise trade. Singapore has been China's largest source of foreign direct investment by annual flows since 2013. It is also the largest recipient in Asia of China's outward direct investment by flows. China will provide US$20 million to support the practical cooperation of Apec.

Prime Minister Wong will next travel to Beijing for a meeting and working lunch with Premier Li Qiang. He will wrap up his trip on Saturday after attending the 33rd Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting. The articles leave open the specific details of the new digital economy and government procurement rules. They do not state when the Free Trade Agreement 4.0 upgrade will be finalized. The text does not specify the exact timeline for the new artificial intelligence cooperation.

Articles.Title: Singapore, China launch FTA upgrade talks as leaders discuss closer AI ties - The Business Times

stories.Headline: South Africa aims to move from hosting data centers to innovating AI technology
stories.Summary:
President Cyril Ramaphosa announced on November 20, 2026, that South Africa intends to become an active participant in the global artificial intelligence value chain. During a working visit to the United States, the president spoke at a fireside chat held at Stanford University in California. He explained that the nation wants to move beyond simply hosting data centers to participate in the actual origination and innovation of technology. This strategic shift aims to ensure that South Africa and the broader African continent help shape emerging technologies instead of just adopting foreign innovations.

This new approach requires that investments in data centers unlock broader opportunities for local researchers, innovators, and businesses. President Ramaphosa noted that global tech giants like Google and Amazon are already establishing data centers in South Africa alongside various domestic firms. He believes the country can integrate into the global ecosystem by leveraging its universities, research institutions, and skilled workforce. Furthermore, the president highlighted that recent improvements in the national electricity supply provide a critical advantage for attracting these digital infrastructure investments.

President Ramaphosa stated that deeper participation in the technology value chain could help the government tackle domestic challenges like inequality and unemployment. He emphasized the need to engage young people in the AI-driven economy while simultaneously recognizing and mitigating the potential risks. The president also called for closer ties with the South African tech diaspora to bring expertise and capital back to young entrepreneurs. He maintained that the country remains open to foreign investment as long as partners help build local capabilities and foster sector collaboration.

Articles.Title: South Africa seeks bigger role in global AI value chain: president - Xinhua

stories.Headline: US stocks plunge as investors sell off artificial intelligence shares
stories.Summary:
United States stocks plunged on Friday, November 20, 2026, as a deepening sell-off in artificial intelligence shares hammered technology stocks. The Nasdaq Composite Index shed 1,261.47 points, or 5.28 percent, to finish at 22,617.73. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 949.73 points, or 1.93 percent, to 48,147.33, while the S&P 500 sank 265.44 points, or 3.70 percent, to 6,910.39. These losses pushed the Dow and S&P 500 into correction territory and marked the worst week for all three indexes since early April 2025.

The technology sector fell 7.11 percent and consumer discretionary dropped 3.50 percent, though consumer staples rose 0.68 percent. Nvidia fell 14.01 percent after reports that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is examining its accounting practices, losing over 40 percent since October 6. Advanced Micro Devices, Micron Technology, and Broadcom all fell over 10 percent, while CoreWeave slumped 12.02 percent. Anthropic fell 8.5 percent to around 89 dollars, and Intuit dropped 12.77 percent while announcing the sale of Mailchimp for about 3.68 billion dollars.

Bénédicte Lowe, an equity derivatives strategist at BNP Paribas, stated that no market can survive a proper unwind of the tech trade. She noted that investors were selling technology shares to determine if the general enthusiasm for artificial intelligence had finally peaked. Meanwhile, the Cboe Volatility Index spiked more than 30 percent to a 52-week high as fear grew. Walmart rose 1.52 percent following higher revenue reports and an increase in its full-year guidance.

Investors fled to government bonds, causing the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield to drop as much as 14 basis points to 4.91 percent. The University of Michigan reported that consumer sentiment rose to 51.5 in November from 48 in October, while inflation expectations fell to 3.7 percent. Market participants are now pricing in a quarter-point rate hike for the Federal Reserve meeting on December 8-9. This expectation follows October meeting minutes showing that almost all officials believe a further increase is appropriate.

stories.Headline: Fiji creates frameworks to regulate artificial intelligence in the civil service
stories.Summary:
The Fijian government began developing three key frameworks on November 20, 2026, to regulate the responsible use of artificial intelligence across the civil service. This initiative is part of a broader digital transformation agenda designed to build a digital economy and improve overall government efficiency. These efforts aim to make public services more accessible to citizens while accelerating the general digitization of various government functions. The government intends to ensure that technological innovation is supported by strict ethical standards, transparency, and accountability.

The project requires the implementation of the Fiji Civil Service AI Policy, the AI Competency Framework, and the AI Governance Framework. These instruments align with the National Digital Strategy 2025-2030, which prioritizes digital infrastructure, inclusion, and innovation-led economic growth. The strategy focuses on smart governance and digital public services to create a more integrated digital government system. This system will include a unified online services portal, stronger cybersecurity capabilities, and improved arrangements for sharing data. A government assessment identified 788 services, with 385 of those targeted for digitization by 2030.

Minister for Communications Ioane Naivalurua stated on Friday that these frameworks would establish clear guidelines for adopting AI across government institutions. He explained that the guidelines would help public servants use the technology responsibly and consistently with public expectations. The minister believes these measures will ensure that AI applications remain aligned with the primary priorities of the government. By doing so, the administration hopes to support innovation while maintaining a high level of institutional accountability.

The digital transformation drive is expected to reduce administrative costs and minimize the amount of paperwork and waiting times for citizens. These improvements are specifically intended to help people living in remote and maritime communities access government services more easily. The government will continue pursuing its goals of smart governance and digital inclusion as outlined in the national strategy. This comprehensive approach seeks to modernize the public sector and foster sustainable economic growth through advanced technology.

Articles.Title: Fiji develops frameworks to guide responsible AI use in public service - Xinhua

stories.Headline: China and Australia plan to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence and green development
stories.Summary:
Chinese Premier Li Qiang met with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Beijing on Friday, November 20, 2026, for the 11th China-Australia Annual Leaders' Meeting. The two leaders discussed ways to strengthen their comprehensive strategic partnership by focusing on shared interests and managing their differences. They aimed to build a foundation for future cooperation as the two nations approach the 55th anniversary of their diplomatic relations next year. The proposed plan requires expanding trade volume and optimizing the structure of commerce between the two countries. Both nations intend to develop new cooperation in emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, new energy vehicles, and green, low-carbon development.

They also seek to enhance investment liberalization and make the upcoming China-Australia Year of Tourism a success. Furthermore, the leaders want to deepen exchanges involving youth, media, think tanks, and local government areas. Premier Li Qiang stated that China is ready to work with Australia to deliver more outcomes and safeguard international fairness. He mentioned that China will strengthen coordination within the UN and APEC to uphold the multilateral system and free trade. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese congratulated China for hosting the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen.

He noted that Australia should take a long-term perspective and not allow differences to disrupt bilateral relations. Albanese expressed a willingness to deepen cooperation in agriculture, energy, and the broader economy. He specifically highlighted the need to accelerate joint efforts in the digital economy and clean energy. The two countries plan to continue their communication through various international frameworks to maintain stability. They will focus on advancing cooperation in these diverse fields to ensure mutual growth and stability.

stories.Headline: Nikkei index plunges over 5 percent amid AI valuation and Anthropic IPO concerns
stories.Summary:
Japan's benchmark Nikkei stock index plunged more than 5 percent on Friday, November 20, 2026. This sharp decline briefly pushed the market to its lowest level since April of the same year. Investors reacted negatively to ongoing concerns regarding the artificial intelligence boom and its current market valuations. The sell-off occurred following significant overnight losses on Wall Street that created widespread market jitters.

The 225-issue Nikkei Stock Average ended the day down 3,007.56 points, which represents a 5.06 percent drop to 56,436.65. Simultaneously, the broader Topix index fell by 148.25 points, or 3.88 percent, to close at 3,674.22. These changes were driven by worries over the initial public offering of Anthropic and the sustainability of AI growth. Every major index tracked in the report showed a substantial decrease in value.

Market analysts stated that the volatility was caused by a combination of AI valuation fears and the Anthropic listing. They explained that the sentiment in Tokyo was heavily influenced by the previous trading sessions in the United States. These experts believe that the sudden drop reflects a broader anxiety about the technology sector. No further actions or future predictions were provided by the officials in the report.

stories.Headline: Singapore integrates embodied AI and robotics into public services and industry
stories.Summary:
Singapore is integrating embodied artificial intelligence into daily life through various autonomous systems and robotics. Starting in early 2027, visitors to Sentosa will use ride-hailing apps to book self-driving minibuses for trips between hotels, attractions, and transport hubs. These eight-passenger vehicles were developed by the Guangzhou-based company WeRide through a collaboration with TADA and the Sentosa Development Corporation. Other initiatives include autonomous construction equipment at the Jurong Innovation District and delivery, cleaning, and security robots in the Punggol Digital District.

The city has also deployed specialized robots for public interaction and maintenance across several high-traffic locations. A 1.27 meter tall humanoid robot named Olly provided directions to commuters at the Little India MRT station from late August to mid-September 2026. In May 2026, a Chinese AI robot dog debuted at the Mandai Wildlife Reserve and Sentosa to tell stories and give directions in English and Chinese. Cleaning robots operate at Changi Airport, while lawn-mowing robots maintain the Singapore Botanic Gardens and autonomous robots patrol the Toa Payoh area.

The Singapore Economic Development Board reported this year that the nation now hosts more than 300 robotics companies. These organizations focus on research, manufacturing, and application development across sectors like healthcare, hospitality, logistics, and advanced manufacturing. Some of these technologies are designed to replace humans in high-risk scenarios, such as the firefighting robotic dog demonstrated on April 9, 2026. The government continues to expand these capabilities through maritime testbeds for autonomous vessels and marine drones.

Articles.Title: LensTalk | Embodied AI takes on daily tasks in Singapore - Xinhua

stories.Headline: New York judge weighs order that Kalshi says could shut its exchange nationwide
stories.Summary:
New York Attorney General Letitia James sued the prediction market Kalshi in July, claiming the company operates an illegal gambling business. US District Judge Vernon Broderick sent this lawsuit back to state court on Thursday, November 19, after finding the federal court lacked jurisdiction. On Friday, November 20, US District Judge Lorna Schofield denied a request from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to stop the state court from ruling. Justice Melissa Crane has now scheduled a hearing for Monday at 11:30 a.m. ET to consider a temporary restraining order.

The attorney general seeks an order to stop Kalshi from offering sports contracts without a license from the New York State Gaming Commission. This legal action targets betting on New York college teams and sports wagering by individuals under 21 years of age. The proposed order covers contracts on sports, culture, elections, and other events offered within or from New York. The lawsuit also seeks the forfeiture of profits, restitution, and various penalties against the company. Kalshi reports having 1.2 million users in New York, an annualized trading volume of $178 billion, and a $22 billion valuation.

Kalshi attorney Sean Murphy and CFTC attorney Andrew Weisberg stated that the order could force the liquidation of all positions and shut down operations nationwide. They argue that because Kalshi is based in New York, any order covering contracts offered from the state would affect all customers. Attorney General representative Kate Rhodes Janofsky told the federal court that there is no evidence of market disruption. Kalshi spokesperson Elisabeth Diana said the company wants to reach a resolution with the Governor and the Attorney General.

The CFTC has sued 12 states, including New York, arguing that federal derivatives law overrides state gambling laws. Recently, a federal appeals court ruled that Kalshi cannot stop Maryland from regulating its sports contracts. Additionally, the Senate passed the DEATH BETS Act to ban contracts regarding war and death. The company continues to fight the New York order to avoid a total exchange shutdown.

Articles.Title: Kalshi fights a New York restraining order it says could shut its exchange nationwide - MLQ.ai

stories.Headline: Lenovo hits record revenue as AI infrastructure demand drives growth
stories.Summary:
Lenovo Group Ltd reported record second-quarter revenue for fiscal year 2026/27, ending on September 30. The company achieved these historic results because the demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure pushed quarterly revenue past the 200 billion yuan threshold for the first time. Total revenue reached 202.9 billion yuan, which is approximately 30.2 billion dollars, representing a 47.8 percent increase year-on-year. Adjusted net income surged 166 percent to 1.4 billion dollars, while the adjusted net margin rose two percentage points to a record 4.5 percent.

The infrastructure solutions group acted as a hyper-growth engine with quarterly revenue of 76.1 billion yuan and operating profit exceeding 7 billion yuan, or 1 billion dollars. AI-related revenue surpassed 10 billion dollars, which is a 79 percent year-on-year increase and accounts for 36 percent of total group revenue. AI server revenue jumped more than 300 percent, and the AI infrastructure backlog climbed to 530 billion yuan. The company generated 1.6 billion dollars in operating cash flow and 1.2 billion dollars in free cash flow.

Chairman and CEO Yang Yuanqing stated that the company delivered an exceptional quarter and successfully transformed from a PC leader into a global full-stack compute leader. He explained that real-world AI adoption is booming and computing demand has not yet peaked as the industry shifts toward parallel training and inference. Yang noted that supply remains the main bottleneck while edge, on-device, and private-domain AI will create new demand. He believes that faster growth in higher-value segments is reshaping the profit mix and helping to mitigate industry cost pressures.

Lenovo is now increasing research and development in edge computing, AI PCs, and next-generation server cooling. The company also confirmed that its first NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks have completed the delivery validation process. Beyond the infrastructure sector, the PC and solutions and services businesses continued to grow steadily. The company intends to balance strong growth and higher component costs through disciplined capital expenditure and credit risk controls for large projects.

stories.Headline: Great Robotics launches NewDawn X integrated robotic platform for minimally invasive surgery
stories.Summary:
Great Robotics presented the NewDawn X all-domain minimally invasive intelligent platform during the COA 2026 orthopedics congress in Guangzhou. This comprehensive system moves beyond standalone product breakthroughs by integrating several specialized robotic tools into one cohesive ecosystem. The platform includes the NewDawn Endo Series active surgical robot and the NewDawn 3D Series mobile imaging robot. It also features the NewDawn Vascular Series intelligent DSA system and the NewDawn META remote robotic surgery system.

This integrated solution requires a combination of physical AI, imaging, and robotics to link image perception with intelligent planning. The system uses master-slave force control to ensure that the robotic arm follows the specific intent of the surgeon. Real-time sensor data and intraoperative imaging create a feedback loop that supports quantitative decisions during medical procedures. Furthermore, the telesurgery system allows high-quality surgical outcomes to be reproduced across different geographic regions.

Professor Zhou, a pioneer of minimally invasive spine surgery in China, described this technological path as quantifiable, traceable, and optimizable. He explained that imaging and robotic control transform surgical maneuvers from experience-based tasks into digital processes. These digital processes can be recorded and reviewed to ensure that medical care is continuously improved over time. This shift reflects a broader trend among APEC economies that are placing more emphasis on digital health and AI-enabled care.

The industry is currently shifting its competitive focus from individual equipment breakthroughs toward the development of entire systems. This transition aims to move new technology from the exhibition floor into actual clinical practice more effectively. By combining various robotic functions, the NewDawn X platform creates a chain of active robotic execution and teleoperation. This approach allows for a more integrated method of delivering complex orthopedic care to patients.

Articles.Title: From one robot to one ecosystem: Physical AI is changing healthcare - China Daily

stories.Headline: Alibaba trains next-generation Qwen AI model on in-house chips
stories.Summary:
Alibaba announced on Thursday that its next-generation Qwen AI model is being trained using in-house chips. This news came during the company's fiscal 2027 second-quarter earnings call. The announcement occurred amid an intensive roll-out of various Chinese AI models. Other major Chinese developers also released new products or updates during the past week. This shift moves competition toward cost, domestic computing adaptation, and post-training optimization.

The T-Head GPU roadmap includes the Zhenwu M890 launching this year and V900 and J900 mass production in 2027. Alibaba Cloud revenue from AI and compute services rose 53 percent, while AI product revenue reached 17.92 billion yuan. New U.S. rules from November 16 and November 19 restrict remote cloud access and overseas foundry production. TSMC and Samsung suspended shipments for nodes 16 nanometers or below, limiting Chinese firms to 28nm and 40nm. Licensing now applies to semiconductor exports to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand.

CEO Wu Yongming stated that domestic computing infrastructure is becoming the supporting base for full-stack AI technology. He said this base will carry workloads for Alibaba and its customers in inference, training, and agentic tasks. Wu noted that capacity expansion in 2027-28 will make the pace of long-term model iteration more controllable. The company revealed that its AI-related annual revenue will top 10 billion dollars. Alibaba also reported that total revenue in the third quarter rose 10 percent year-on-year.

Baidu released the Ernie 5.5 Flash Preview with 280 billion parameters and a 1 million token context window. Tencent's WorkBuddy agent topped 10 million daily active users and 100 trillion daily tokens. Zhipu AI released GLM-5.3, which improved coding capability by 50 percent over the previous GLM-5.2 version. Databricks data from November 2 shows GLM-series models account for over 60 percent of open-weight token usage. The Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs said U.S. measures infringe on rights and undermine global supply chain stability.

The U.S. Department of Commerce is investigating Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company, for possible export control violations. Applied Materials previously paid a 252.5 million dollar penalty for illegal equipment exports to China via South Korea. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized Nvidia's internal controls, suggesting executives would be dismissed if Nvidia were a bank. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang denied allegations of chip diversion before his resignation. The U.S. government is now seeking to increase statutory caps on fines for violating export controls.

The U.S. Senate is considering semiconductor tracking mechanisms and congressional review of licenses for advanced AI chip sales. A defense bill scheduled for the end of the year may further restrict cloud computing and equipment exports. The Trump administration has shown internal disagreements between the Treasury and Commerce departments regarding the timing of rules. It remains open whether China will retaliate by restricting rare earth exports as it has done previously. Nvidia expects to maintain solid business performance because AI semiconductor demand continues to far exceed the supply.

stories.Headline: Huawei Launches AI-Focused Smartphone Sub-Brand OSTA
stories.Summary:
Huawei Technologies Co. Ltd. launched a new smartphone sub-brand called OSTA on Friday, November 20, 2026. This move marks a return to a multibrand strategy for the company six years after it sold Honor. The debut device is the AI-focused O1 Pro, which is designed to compete in the modern technology market. This new handset is available at various price points depending on the specific hardware specifications.

The OSTA O1 Pro runs on the HarmonyOS operating system and features an AI assistant with context-based recommendations. It offers over 2,100 system capabilities to enhance the overall user experience for its customers. Prices for the new device start at 5,499 yuan, which is approximately 825 dollars. The highest-specification version of the phone is priced at 8,799 yuan, and these rates apply through December 31.

Richard Yu, who serves as the chairman of the consumer business group at Huawei, led the announcement. He stated that OSTA intends to become a pioneering technology brand that consumers will favor during the AI era. This strategic expansion comes as Huawei leads the smartphone market in China with a 21.1 percent share for the third quarter. The company is leveraging its strong market position to integrate advanced artificial intelligence into its mobile hardware.

stories.Headline: US authorities approve export of nearly 880,000 AI chips to Chinese companies
stories.Summary:
United States authorities approved the export or transfer of nearly 880,000 advanced artificial intelligence chips to various Chinese companies. These approvals were granted out of a much larger pool of applications covering 3.4 million chips in total. House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast released these specific records on Thursday using powers from the U.S. Export Control Reform Act. The disclosed documents include an approval tally dated May 11 and cover applications from Nvidia Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.

The approved shipments were intended for several major Chinese firms including Alibaba, Tencent, Baidu, and BYD. However, the released records indicate that many of these approved shipments had not actually been delivered to the buyers. This situation occurs as the Bureau of Industry and Security issued new rules on November 16, 2026, to restrict exports. These updated regulations target advanced AI chips and server exports to five different countries, which includes Malaysia, along with other restrictive measures.

Chairman Brian Mast is the official responsible for releasing the records to highlight the current state of chip transfers. He provided the data to show the gap between the number of chips requested and those actually cleared for export. The disclosure comes at a time when members of Congress are pushing for much tighter controls on chip sales to China. These officials believe that stricter oversight is necessary to manage the flow of advanced technology into the Chinese market.

The broader context involves a growing effort by the United States government to limit the computing power available to Chinese tech giants. The new rules from the Bureau of Industry and Security also include restrictions on the use of cloud services. These measures are designed to prevent the acquisition of high-end hardware that could be used for sensitive military or intelligence purposes. Future actions will likely focus on closing loopholes that allowed millions of chips to be requested by foreign entities.

stories.Headline: US voters demand control over AI data center construction as electricity and water concerns grow
stories.Summary:
The current race to build the necessary infrastructure for artificial intelligence is facing a significant political reckoning across the United States. Many voters are now demanding much greater control over the development of data centers because they are worried about the local impact. These citizens are specifically concerned that the massive construction projects will lead to higher electricity bills and depleted water supplies. This backlash has emerged as the rapid expansion of AI facilities begins to clash with the needs of local communities. It is clear that the primary changes requested involve stricter oversight of how these sprawling construction projects are approved and managed. Voters want to ensure that the energy and water demands of AI do not compromise the resources available to residents. The tension centers on balancing the technological ambitions of the country with the practical sustainability of regional infrastructure. Those responsible for the pushback are the voters who feel that their concerns are being ignored by developers and policymakers.

While the text does not provide direct quotes, it indicates that these individuals are voicing their opposition to the unchecked growth of data centers. They believe that the environmental and financial costs of the AI boom are becoming too high for the average citizen to bear. The public is calling for a more transparent process that prioritizes community stability over corporate expansion. More to follow.

stories.Headline: House committees warn US companies against using Chinese open weight AI models
stories.Summary:
The House Homeland Security Committee and the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party released a report on November 20, 2026, regarding American companies using Chinese open weight artificial intelligence. This joint investigation found that firms like Airbnb, DoorDash, and Anysphere, the owner of the Cursor coding platform, embedded these models into their tech stacks for inventory, coding, and customer assistance. The report warns that allowing these models to take root could cost taxpayers billions of dollars and take years to resolve, similar to the threats posed by Huawei and ZTE. The 50-page document proposes twelve policy recommendations, including the creation of an American open-weight AI initiative and a standard for sourcing models. It suggests establishing an AI bill of materials and banning China-developed models from sensitive critical infrastructure and federal contract work.

The report also calls for the systematic evaluation of Chinese models to mitigate risks. These changes aim to prevent the long-term integration of foreign technology that could compromise national security. Representatives Andrew Garbarino and John Moolenaar, both from New York, authored the report based on agency advisories, classified briefings, and hearings. They stated that the investigation revealed risks that national security officials and American businesses can no longer afford to downplay or overlook. The lawmakers noted that while the United States invests billions in super intelligence, Beijing is utilizing stolen intelligence to close the technological gap.

They highlighted that Chinese developers used fraudulent accounts and proxy networks to replicate the capabilities of American frontier models. Cybersecurity expert Mark Montgomery of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies explained that China is expanding global dependence on its open-source AI to kill competition. He noted that companies often ignore safety and security issues to achieve lower front end costs, a strategy that Chinese leaders understand well. Because American firms like OpenAI and Anthropic dominate the frontier model space, China is focusing on the low cost open-source marketplace. The report emphasizes the urgent need for the United States to compete more seriously in this specific sector.

stories.Headline: NTT DATA becomes official AI consulting partner of the Nitto ATP Finals
stories.Summary:
NTT DATA became a Gold Partner of the Nitto ATP Finals, serving as Official AI Consulting Partner and Official Technology Consulting Partner, the company announced on November 12, 2026. The 2026 tournament will take place from November 15 to 22 at Inalpi Arena in Turin, Italy. NTT DATA is a global leader in AI, digital business and technology services. The partnership gives NTT DATA a global stage to showcase how AI, data and technology can support human potential. Elite tennis brings together skill, judgment and the ability to adapt under pressure.

NTT DATA will host a Tech Corner in Turin where visitors can see computer vision, Physical AI and advanced AI infrastructure applied to real-world scenarios. Those scenarios include monitoring, safety, construction and humanoid robotics. The space will also house the Mental Economy Gym, powered by Formula Medicine, an Italian company specializing in sports medicine and human performance. Guests there can take on digital challenges that measure indicators such as concentration, reaction and mental workload. At the Fan Village court, NTT DATA will showcase an on-court experience presented by FITP, combining cognitive and physical monitoring with AI-powered computer vision.

Kazuhiko Nakayama, President and CEO of NTT DATA Group, said what makes sport extraordinary is ultimately human, citing the ambition to push boundaries, the courage to take risks and the determination to achieve more. He said technology has the power to unlock even greater possibilities by helping people see what was previously invisible and discover new ways to improve. As an AI Consulting Partner of the Nitto ATP Finals, he said, NTT DATA wants to celebrate human potential while demonstrating how technology can expand what people can achieve. He said NTT DATA combines AI capabilities with deep industry expertise to help clients transform their businesses and create new value. The partnership is the latest in a series of sporting partnerships that bring NTT DATA's global brand positioning statement, "Intelligence to Impact," to life.

IT Brief UK reported that the partnership places the technology group alongside one of men's tennis's best-known season-ending events. The report said NTT DATA will use the tournament to show how AI, data and related systems can generate performance insights and support decision-making under pressure. IT Brief UK said the announcement reflects a wider trend in professional sport, where tournaments, teams and governing bodies use technology partnerships to enhance fan experiences and collect more detailed information on athlete preparation and match play. The report said tennis has become a testing ground for data-led analysis, with systems used across officiating, broadcast coverage and training. IT Brief UK said the demonstrations will place tools used in industrial and operational settings into a consumer-facing environment, linking them to measurable human activity rather than back-office processes.

NTT DATA is a $30+ billion business and technology services leader serving 75% of the Fortune Global 100. It describes itself as one of the world's leading AI and digital infrastructure providers, with capabilities in enterprise-scale AI, cloud, security, connectivity, data centers and application services. As a Global Top Employer, NTT DATA has experts in more than 70 countries. NTT DATA is part of NTT Group, which invests over $3 billion each year in R&D. NTT DATA said it will continue to build on these efforts, using sport as a platform to demonstrate how AI and technology can enhance human potential and create meaningful impact beyond sport.

NTT DATA said the partnership reflects its belief that intelligence comes not only from AI and technology, but also from human expertise and deep industry understanding. It said what matters is how these strengths are brought together to create meaningful impact for clients and society. NTT DATA offers clients access to a robust ecosystem of innovation centers as well as established and start-up partners. The company said its consulting and industry solutions help organizations and society move confidently and sustainably into the digital future. NTT DATA said it is committed to accelerating client success and positively impacting society through responsible innovation.

stories.Headline: NTT DATA finds Asia Pacific clients more open to outcome-based AI deals than Western markets
stories.Summary:
Nitin Bajaj, the global head of AI strategy and product at NTT DATA, announced at the NTT R&D Forum 2026 in Tokyo that Asia Pacific clients are more open to outcome-based AI deals than those in Europe or North America. This shift is part of a broader strategy called services as software, where AI agents perform tasks that were previously billed by the number of hours or people assigned to the work. The company is moving away from traditional headcount models to focus on measurable results, noting that this appetite for performance-based arrangements has grown over the last two years. The new approach requires different pricing models, including consumption-based fees for high-volume tasks and fees tied to specific results, such as increasing system uptime from 90% to 98.5%. Some contracts involve revenue or profit sharing, such as taking a percentage of profits from a telecommunications call center that exceeds a baseline for new customers.

Bajaj noted that NTT DATA ran over 600 AI pilot projects in 2024, which eventually led to 1,350 paid projects last year. While only about 20% of those specific pilots went into production, the region now accounts for 15 to 20% of pilot volume and is growing quickly. Bajaj explained that the openness in Asia Pacific stems from a diverse mix of frontier, privately developed, and Chinese open-weight models, as well as specific regional capital structures. He admitted that outcome-based contracts are difficult to manage because providers cannot control every variable within a client's business that might affect the final result. He also mentioned that many AI projects fail due to fragmented data in old systems rather than the models themselves, citing estimates that 80% of such projects fail to deliver.

To improve efficiency, the company uses its Silicon Valley firm, AIVista, to reduce document processing costs from a benchmark of 43 cents to about 17 cents. The company is expanding its partnerships with hyperscalers like Amazon Web Services, which has significant influence in the Asia Pacific banking market, and Databricks. NTT DATA is also strengthening its relationship with Google Cloud and expects to have more than 5,000 engineers certified on the Gemini Enterprise platform within a few months. By integrating these tools into a full software stack, the company aims to guarantee the variables that impact client outcomes. This strategy allows them to offer sovereign AI solutions that keep data and control within a specific organization or country.

stories.Headline: Nvidia corrects its AI model with 20,000 training examples and raises its coding score
stories.Summary:
Nvidia used 20,000 training examples to correct mistakes made by its artificial intelligence model, and the effort produced a measurable jump in the model's coding score, according to The New Stack. The report, published on November 21, 2026, describes the work as a fix for errors the AI had been making rather than a new model release. The article gives the size of the training set as 20,000 examples and ties that figure directly to the improvement in coding performance. It does not name the specific model, the benchmark used for the coding score, or the exact before and after numbers.

The change the article describes is a training intervention built on those 20,000 examples, which were used to correct the model's mistakes rather than to expand its general knowledge. The result reported is a jump in the coding score, which the article presents as the main outcome of the effort. Beyond the 20,000 figure and the November 21, 2026 publication date, the article supplies no further numbers, no version names and no timeline for the work. It also does not say whether the corrected model was released publicly or kept internal.

The article does not identify individual Nvidia employees, executives or researchers as responsible for the work, and it carries no direct statements from the company about the project. Responsibility for the training effort is attributed to Nvidia as an organization, with no named spokesperson and no quoted explanation of why the mistakes occurred. Because no one is quoted, there is no paraphrased comment from the company on the method, the cost or the results. The article likewise does not say whether Nvidia described the score jump as expected or surprising.

The context the article provides is limited to the framing that Nvidia fixed its AI's mistakes using 20,000 training examples and saw its coding score rise as a result. It does not place the work against competing models, prior Nvidia releases or independent evaluations, and it does not say what happens next. No follow-up release, publication of the training data or further testing is mentioned in the article. Readers looking for the model's name, the benchmark or the size of the score gain will not find them in the piece as published.
